# chat-demo

English | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)

A static chat demo powered by the DeepSeek API. No application backend is required: the browser connects directly to the configured API service.

You can [try the app online](https://deepseek-ai.github.io/chat-demo/) or download the archive from [Releases](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-chat-demo/releases), extract it, and double-click `index.html` to use it locally without installation or a build. Enter your API key in Settings before your first chat.

## Getting started

Install Node.js 22.12+ and pnpm, then run:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/deepseek-ai/chat-demo.git
cd chat-demo
pnpm install
pnpm dev
```

Open http://localhost:8090.

To build the static site:

```sh
pnpm build
```

The output is written to `dist/`. Deploy it to a static web server or open `dist/index.html` directly. Opening the file directly requires browser support for storage on `file://` pages and an API service that permits their cross-origin requests.

## Features

- Multiple conversations with automatic titles, renaming, and deletion; edit prompts, regenerate replies, and switch between message branches.
- Streaming replies, deep thinking, smart search, link reading, and source citations; stop generation or continue eligible replies.
- Upload, paste, or drag and drop attachments; use voice input and read replies aloud. A live audio spectrum appears in the first row of the input area while recording on mobile.
- Markdown, syntax highlighting, KaTeX math, and Mermaid diagrams.
- Simplified Chinese and English, light and dark themes, mobile layouts, location settings, and chat history import and export.

## Data and storage

Your API key and settings are stored in the browser's localStorage. Conversations and original attachments are stored in IndexedDB. Local data is isolated by browser profile and site origin. Sending messages, uploading attachments, and using speech features sends the relevant content to the configured API service.

History import and export in Settings use ZIP archives. After confirmation and successful validation, importing replaces all local conversations and attachments. Exports include conversations and locally available original images, but exclude API keys, settings, and original non-image attachments. See the [history import/export documentation (Chinese)](src/services/chat/history/README.md) for the archive format and preservation details.

Settings → Data → Delete all chats clears all local conversations, original attachments, and unsent drafts after confirmation. It stops ongoing replies and returns to a new chat. Your API key and settings are preserved; files already uploaded to the API service are not deleted.

## Development

| Command       | Description                  |
| ------------- | ---------------------------- |
| `pnpm dev`    | Start the development server |
| `pnpm build`  | Build into `dist/`           |
| `pnpm type`   | Run TypeScript type checks   |
| `pnpm lint`   | Lint with oxlint             |
| `pnpm format` | Format with oxfmt            |

[rspack.config.ts](rspack.config.ts) uses `https://api.deepseek.com` by default. Use `createConfig({ apiOrigin, devServer })` to customize the API origin and development server proxy.

Chat uses `deepseek-flash` by default through Anthropic-compatible Messages / Files APIs. Speech features use ASR / TTS endpoints. Requests include extensions for search, link reading, titles, and `latest_reminder`, so the configured service must support the corresponding capabilities. Supported attachment formats are determined by server-side validation.

```text
src/
  app/                 Application layout, themes, and global styles
  components/          Chat, settings, Markdown, and other UI components
  i18n/                English and Chinese translations
  services/
    api/               API requests, SSE, and protocol types
    chat/              Conversations, message branches, storage, and history import/export
    markdown/          Markdown parsing, syntax highlighting, and diagrams
    speech/            Audio recording and read-aloud playback
  utils/               Shared utilities
```

## License

[MIT](LICENSE). The build copies the license to `dist/LICENSE`; include it when distributing the app. Third-party dependencies are subject to their own licenses.

Battery levels of your wireless mouse, headset, keyboard and controller, right on the Windows taskbar.

![Wireless Battery on the taskbar](docs/screenshot.png)

> **Just want it working?** Download **[WirelessBattery-Setup](https://github.com/krisgfx9/Wireless-Device-Battery-Monitor/releases/latest)** from the latest release, run it and click through. That's it.
>
> **Experienced users** can grab the portable zip, use the [command-line options](#command-line), or [build it from source](#build) with `make` or `build.bat`.
>
> **Like it?** Wireless Battery is free and open source. If it saves you a trip into vendor software, you can support it on [Ko-fi](https://ko-fi.com/krisgfx), [PayPal](https://www.paypal.com/paypalme/krisgfx) or [GitHub Sponsors](https://github.com/sponsors/krisgfx9). It helps me keep my apps free alongside my studies. Not able to donate? A ⭐ star, sharing it, or reporting an unsupported device with a `--dump` helps just as much.

- **Tiny**: a ~350 KB app using about 2 MB of RAM. It's plain C++/Win32, with no runtime and no background service, and installs in seconds without admin rights.
- **No vendor software needed**: it talks to the devices directly. G HUB, Synapse, iCUE, GG and NGenuity can stay closed (or keep running; they don't conflict).
- **Many brands**: Logitech, Razer, SteelSeries, Corsair, HyperX, Glorious, Jabra, JBL, PlayStation and Xbox controllers, Samsung Galaxy Buds, any Bluetooth device Windows knows a battery level for, and every headset the bundled [HeadsetControl](https://github.com/Sapd/HeadsetControl) supports.

## Display

**On the taskbar (default):** `🎧 30%  🖱 93%` next to the notification area, drawn with the Windows icon font.
- **Low battery:** a red number means 15% or less.
- **Charging:** a blue ⚡ appears next to the number.
- **Asleep:** dimmed text means the device is asleep and the last known value is shown.
- **Theme:** it follows light/dark mode and DPI scaling.
- **Transparent taskbar themes** (e.g. Windhawk's Taskbar Styler): turn on *Background behind taskbar text* in the menu to keep the text readable over the wallpaper.
- **Several monitors:** the widget shows on every monitor's taskbar, next to its clock, so it stays visible while a game runs fullscreen. *Show the widget on* in the menu picks *All monitors*, *Main monitor only*, or one display (e.g. only *Display 3*).

**Tray icons:** one icon per device with the number drawn in it, plus a "Low battery" notification at 15%. The app switches to this automatically when the taskbar is vertical or can't be found.

Hover for details. Click for the menu: every device (click one to hide or show it), display mode, *Refresh now*, *Start with Windows*, and *Exit*. Levels refresh every 60 seconds, and right away when a device is plugged in or the PC wakes up.

## Install

[![Latest version](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/krisgfx9/Wireless-Device-Battery-Monitor?label=latest%20version&style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/krisgfx9/Wireless-Device-Battery-Monitor/releases/latest)

1. Download **`WirelessBattery-Setup-<version>.exe`** from the [latest release](https://github.com/krisgfx9/Wireless-Device-Battery-Monitor/releases/latest).
2. Run it and click through. It needs **no administrator rights** and **nothing else installed**: no
   runtimes, no drivers, no vendor apps. HeadsetControl comes bundled.

The installer adds a Start menu entry and an uninstaller (*Settings → Apps*), and can start the app
when you sign in. Prefer no installer? Download `WirelessBattery-<version>-portable.zip`, unzip it
anywhere and run `WirelessBattery.exe`.

**Notes:**
- **SmartScreen warning:** the exe is not code-signed, so Windows may say "Windows protected your PC". Click *More info → Run anyway*, or build it yourself.
- **Tray-icon mode on Windows 11:** new tray icons go to the `^` overflow. Drag them onto the taskbar or enable them in *Settings → Personalization → Taskbar → Other system tray icons*.
- **Keeping the app away from a device:** if a device misbehaves while the app is running, list it in the registry string `IgnoreDevices` under `HKCU\Software\WirelessBattery` as `VID:PID` pairs (hex, separated by commas, e.g. `28BD:0947, 1234:ABCD`; `--dump` shows the ids). The app then never opens it. Drawing tablets are skipped automatically.

## Command line

```
WirelessBattery.exe --list     # print every device and its battery level, then exit
WirelessBattery.exe --dump     # every HID collection, HID devices that could not be opened, all USB devices (also ones
                               # without a HID interface) and Bluetooth devices; also saved to %TEMP%\WirelessBattery-dump.txt
WirelessBattery.exe --report   # open the "Request support for a device" window
WirelessBattery.exe --quit     # close the running instance
```

**Device not shown?** Right-click the widget or tray icon and choose **Request support for a device...**. Pick the device, check
what will be sent (it is shown word for word: the device name, its type, its USB/HID ids and interface layout, and your optional
name and notes) and click **Send**. It goes on the public list at [krisgfx.com/tools](https://krisgfx.com/tools/#requested) and
opens or updates a GitHub issue. **Copy full report** puts the complete `--dump` on the clipboard for the issue. This window is
the only place the app connects to the internet, and only when you click Send.

## Build

You need [MinGW-w64](https://www.mingw-w64.org/), e.g. from [MSYS2](https://www.msys2.org/) (`pacman -S mingw-w64-x86_64-gcc make`).

```
make            # MSYS2 / any shell with make
build.bat       # plain cmd with g++ and windres on PATH
```

To build the installer and portable zip, install [Inno Setup](https://jrsoftware.org/isinfo.php) and run
`powershell -File installer\build-installer.ps1 -Version 1.0.0`. It downloads the pinned
HeadsetControl release and verifies its checksum. GitHub Actions does all of this automatically:
pushing a tag like `v1.0.0` publishes a release with the installer, the portable zip and the
HeadsetControl source (as its GPL license requires).

`WirelessBattery.exe` on its own also works. Without `headsetcontrol.exe` next to it (or on `PATH`) you
just lose the extra headsets.

## Linux (experimental)

A Linux build sits alongside the Windows app. It uses the same vendor drivers with a hidraw-based
HID backend and a GTK4 StatusNotifierItem tray icon; the Windows code path is unchanged.
All Linux-only files are in `linux/` and `src/linux/`, and `build-linux.sh` builds it (Windows keeps using `build.bat`).

| | Fedora | Ubuntu / Debian |
|---|---|---|
| Compiler & make | `sudo dnf install gcc-c++ make` | `sudo apt install g++ make` |
| GTK4 + Cairo | `sudo dnf install gtk4-devel cairo-devel` | `sudo apt install libgtk-4-dev libcairo2-dev` |

No extra HID library is needed (hidraw is used directly).

```sh
./build-linux.sh
./build-linux.sh test         # unit test for the HID report-descriptor parser
./wireless-battery --list     # print detected levels and exit
./wireless-battery --dump     # list HID collections
./wireless-battery --quit     # close the running tray instance
```

HID access needs a udev rule, otherwise the app starts but finds no devices:

```sh
sudo cp linux/99-wireless-battery.rules /etc/udev/rules.d/
sudo udevadm control --reload-rules && sudo udevadm trigger
# log out and back in
```

The tray icon works natively on KDE Plasma; GNOME needs an AppIndicator host such as
`gnome-shell-extension-appindicator`. The optional launcher is `linux/wireless-battery.desktop`
(install it plus `linux/wireless-battery.svg` and the binary into `~/.local/`).

Phase 1 covers Logitech, Razer, SteelSeries, Corsair, HyperX, PlayStation, Cooler Master, Glorious,
Finalmouse and the shared Kysona/Pulsar/ATK/G-Wolves protocols. Bluetooth/UPower fallbacks, HeadsetControl and
the remaining vendors are planned follow-up phases.

## Limitations

- **Primary monitor only:** the taskbar widget sits on the primary monitor's taskbar.
- **Crowded taskbars:** with a very full centered Windows 11 taskbar, the app buttons can reach the widget. On Windows 10 the task-button area is narrowed automatically.
- **Phones:** read from a file Phone Link writes for the Start menu companion card, which is not a documented API and may change with Phone Link updates. The phone shows while Phone Link reports it as connected; a card older than 3 hours is shown dimmed. Charging state is not available there.
- **Sleeping devices:** a device that is asleep may not answer. Its last value stays visible, dimmed. Logitech receivers drop sleeping devices from the link, so their last value is kept for 30 minutes.

Support is for Nordic 54L report `07` and legacy VT3 Pro `BB`; CH584 report `08`, office MT/M-series mice and other firmware protocols are not covered by this driver.

## How it works

Each vendor driver in [`src/drivers/`](src/drivers) recognises its devices by USB vendor and product ID, and only ever sends read-only battery queries. Unknown devices are never written to. The generic fallbacks (HID battery usage, Bluetooth, XInput, HeadsetControl) only look at devices no vendor driver has claimed.

The taskbar widget is a layered child window of `Shell_TrayWnd`, placed left of `TrayNotifyWnd`. If Explorer restarts, it is re-created.

items.description: Rewrite your whole app in Rust, one piece at a time, checked against the original's recorded behavior at every step. CLIs, HTTP servers and libraries in TypeScript, Python, C, Go, Ruby and Java.
items.readme:
rust-anything

Rewrite your whole app in Rust. Keep it working the whole way.

CLIs, servers and libraries, piece by piece, checked against the original at every step.

up to 20x faster · 38,251 recorded cases replayed · 0 mismatches · one command

**Rewrite your whole app in Rust, one piece at a time.** rust-anything records what your TypeScript/JavaScript, Python, C, Go, Ruby or Java app does today, then checks every piece of the Rust rewrite against that recording before it moves on, until the app is pure Rust. CLIs, HTTP servers and libraries; your coding agent (or you) writes the Rust. It can only catch what the recording covers: see [What it can't catch](#what-it-cant-catch). Only need the slow part fast? Port just that, one hot path at a time: | Real workload, same results as the original | Original | With rust-anything | | --- | ---: | ---: | | x18n's sidebar search, 50,000 keys (TypeScript, Node) | 10 ms per query | **0.5 ms: 20x faster** | | The same search in the browser (wasm, one thread) | 10 ms | **0.95 ms: 11.5x** | | `slugify` over 20,000 strings (Python) | 98 ms | **17x faster** | | `Shellwords.shellescape` from Ruby's standard library, 50,000 values | 88 ms | **11.8x faster** | | `Slugify` over 50,000 strings (Go) | 49 ms | **4x faster** | | `slugify` over 50,000 strings (Java) | 43 ms | **3x faster** |

Measured on 4 cores; every number has a benchmark in [`demo/`](./demo) that first checks the results are identical. Calling Rust once per small function is usually *slower* than a JIT; rust-anything finds the loop worth moving, and moves it. > rust-anything is an independent project, not affiliated with or endorsed by the Rust Project > or the Rust Foundation. "Rust" is a trademark of the Rust Foundation. ## Quick start Paste this into Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or Gemini CLI and let your agent install it: ```text Install rust-anything: run `cargo install rust-anything`, then `rust-anything setup`. Tell me when to restart you. ``` Or yourself: ```sh cargo install rust-anything # from crates.io rust-anything setup # registers it with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and Gemini CLI ``` No Rust toolchain yet? Prebuilt binaries for macOS, Linux and Windows are attached to each [GitHub release](https://github.com/erkamyaman/rust-anything/releases), and for JavaScript projects `npm install -g rust-anything` installs the same binary. In Claude Code you can also install it as a plugin (the MCP server and the skill; the CLI above must be on your `PATH`): ```text /plugin install rust-anything --marketplace erkamyaman/rust-anything ``` `setup` adds the MCP server to each agent it finds and installs the workflow skill where the agent reads skills. It keeps your other settings, is safe to run again, and `--remove` undoes it. Then ask your agent, for example: - *"Rewrite this CLI in Rust with rust-anything, end to end, and prove it behaves the same."* - *"This search feels slow. Profile it with rust-anything and move the hot loop to Rust."* - *"Plan a migration of `src/parser/` to Rust with rust-anything; port the first unit and prove it."* - *"Bench the Rust port in `rust/text-rs` against the original and tell me whether to ship it."* ### Works with | Agent | `rust-anything setup` adds | | --- | --- | | Claude Code | MCP server in `~/.claude.json`, skill in `~/.claude/skills/` | | Codex | MCP server in `~/.codex/config.toml`, skill in `~/.codex/skills/` | | Cursor | MCP server in `~/.cursor/mcp.json` | | Gemini CLI | MCP server in `~/.gemini/settings.json` | | Any other MCP client | add `rust-anything mcp` as a stdio server by hand (see [Install](#install)) | Before changing a file that exists, `setup` saves a copy beside it (`.rust-anything.bak`). Or run the steps yourself:

```sh rust-anything profile . -- node bench.mjs # what is hot, and who calls it rust-anything bridge . src/fuzzy.ts --batch fuzzyScore:text # write src/port.rs (or let your agent), then: rust-anything record rust/fuzzy-rs && rust-anything build rust/fuzzy-rs rust-anything diff rust/fuzzy-rs # every recorded case must match rust-anything bench rust/fuzzy-rs # faster? the verdict says rust-anything gate rust/fuzzy-rs # done means this passes ``` rust-anything does not translate code: your coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, ...) or you write the Rust. rust-anything supplies what an agent cannot guess reliably: where the time goes, what to port first and in which order, a bridge so the rest of the code calls the Rust with its API unchanged, the exact behavior the port must match, a safe way to ship it, and a gate that says when a port is done. ## Languages | Language | Unit | Bridge | Recorded and replayed by | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | TypeScript/JavaScript | folder or file | napi-rs or wasm-bindgen with a generated binary wire; classes and async included | Node, running the `.ts` sources | | Python | package or module | PyO3 (abi3), direct conversion, typed exceptions | Python, importing the original | | C | `.c` file | `extern "C"` functions with the original names and a header | the original compiled to a shared library, called through ctypes, one fork per case | | Go | package | typed cgo calls and a generated binary wire, in a package with the original API | a generated Go driver, built as its own module | | Ruby | file or folder of module functions | a magnus extension under the original modules | a generated Ruby driver | | Java | package of `public static` methods | typed JNI and a generated binary wire, in wrapper classes with the original methods | a generated reflection driver | | PHP (preview) | folder of functions and `public static` methods | coming next: PHP FFI over a C ABI | whole apps today: `app record`, `app replay` and the front door, for CLIs and servers (`php -S`) | | C# (preview) | folder of `public static` methods | coming next: P/Invoke over a C ABI | whole apps today: `app record`, `app replay` and the front door, for CLIs and ASP.NET servers (`dotnet .dll`) | Every language except C also gets batch classes (`--batch`): the items cross once and stay in Rust, and each call runs over all of them on all cores. The language is detected from the repository (`go.mod`, `pom.xml`, a `.csproj` or `.sln`, `pyproject.toml`, `Gemfile`, `composer.json`, `package.json`, else the most common source files); `--lang` overrides it. Types come from the source: TS types, Python hints, C, Go, Java and C# signatures, Ruby YARD tags, PHP types and phpdoc; untyped parameters used as numbers are inferred as numbers. PHP is in preview: `analyze` plans a PHP app (Composer packages and PSR-4 autoloading, risks such as loose comparison and integer overflow into floats, Composer packages mapped to crates), and a PHP CLI or server can be recorded, replayed and put behind a Rust front door. Porting its units into Rust through PHP's FFI is the next step ([issue #2](https://github.com/erkamyaman/rust-anything/issues/2)). C# is in preview the same way: `analyze` reads `.csproj` projects and their NuGet packages (mapped to crates), resolves `using` directives to folders, and flags what C# does differently (`decimal`, `dynamic`, LINQ's deferred queries, `Task`, `lock`, reflection). A C# CLI or ASP.NET server can be recorded, replayed and put behind a Rust front door; porting units through P/Invoke comes next. ## How it works ``` profile ──> analyze ──> bridge ──> record ──> port.rs ──> diff ──> bench ──> shadow ──> gate where the what to the Rust what the you or every faster? both side done means time goes port first crate and original your agent recorded the by side in this passes wrapper does write it case verdict production ``` The original stays the source of truth: `record` runs it on edge cases (and your own inputs) and saves what it returns or throws; `diff` replays every case against the Rust; nothing ships until they all match and `gate` passes. Callers keep the original API throughout. A whole app goes through the same loop unit by unit, inside a frame that proves the whole program ([Port a whole app](#port-a-whole-app)): ``` analyze --whole-app ──> app record ──> app front-door ──> per unit: the loop above, then app wire ──> app lift shape, every what the app Rust owns the gate passes, so the unit answers in pure Rust, dependency, the does from the entry point; the Rust: replay 100%, fallback rate down proved by decisions to make outside original answers replay ``` ## The loop | Step | Command | What it does | | --- | --- | --- | | 0. Profile | `rust-anything profile -- node bench.mjs` | Runs a real workload under the language's profiler (node, cProfile, `go test` pprof, JFR, a Ruby tracer): hot functions by inclusive time, their callers, and which loops to batch; flags code that is already compiled (numba, Cython, JAX), where Rust gains little | | 1. Plan | `rust-anything analyze ` | Units, port order, risks with `file:line`, bridge per unit, dependency-to-crate fit, best first ports; `--whole-app` adds entry points and shape, every dependency (imported or declared) with its crate, pieces (units that import each other move together) and numbered decisions with a recommended answer | | 2. Bridge | `rust-anything bridge ` | Crate with the bindings (`lib.rs`, plus the wrapper the source language loads) and stubs to port (`port.rs`); `--batch fn:param` adds a class that keeps many `param` values in Rust | | 3. Record | `rust-anything record ` | Runs the original on generated edge cases (non-ASCII, emoji, `-0`, `NaN`, ints where floats are expected, ...) and on every semantic trap in every parameter (string length and case, signed division, overflow edges, float printing, map and sort order), and saves `cases.jsonl`; `--float-tolerance 1e-9` lets floats match within that share for numeric code | | 3. Build | `rust-anything build ` | Builds the Rust side: `.node`, wasm package, Python extension or shared library | | 3. Diff | `rust-anything diff ` | Replays the recorded cases against Rust, called the way the original's callers call it; lists mismatches | | 3. Bench | `rust-anything bench ` | Times the recorded cases on the original and on Rust, bridge included | | 4. Shadow | `rust-anything shadow ` | Drop-in that runs both, returns the original's result, reports mismatches; `RUST_ANYTHING_MODE=old\|shadow\|new` | | 5. Gate | `rust-anything gate ` | fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, tests, `unsafe` audit, nothing unported, a recorded failing case for every error path of the original, no `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!` where the original returns an error (unless marked `// INFALLIBLE: `), build, API, behavior | | Agents | `rust-anything setup` | Registers the MCP server (`rust-anything mcp`, every step as a tool) and the workflow skill ([`skills/rust-anything/SKILL.md`](./skills/rust-anything/SKILL.md)) with your coding agents | ## Port a whole app The goal is a pure Rust app that behaves like the original, with the original kept as reference. Your agent writes the Rust; rust-anything orders the work, scaffolds it, and proves every step. The [whole-app skill](./skills/rust-anything/whole-app.md) walks the agent through it, starting with the decisions only you can make: - **Grilling**: the agent asks in rounds, each question with its recommended answer, until every decision the port depends on is settled, and writes each one as an ADR in `rust/DECISIONS.md`, with `rust/GLOSSARY.md` mapping the original's terms to Rust names. - **Research**: background agents read each dependency's primary sources and write `rust/research/.md`, with every semantic trap they found. - **Across sessions**: `rust/MAP.md` lists every unit with its state; a session claims one unit before it starts, and each checkpoint leaves a `rust/HANDOFF.md` for the next session. Units in one wave can be ported in parallel by subagents. - **Cutover**: the agent does what it can and writes `rust/cutover.sh`, an interactive script for the steps only you can do (deploys, DNS, secrets), with a way back at each step. Grilling, research and these practices are adapted from [Matt Pocock's skills](https://github.com/mattpocock/skills). Plan first: `rust-anything analyze . --whole-app` adds the app's shape (CLI, server or library) and entry points, every external dependency (imported or declared) with its Rust crate and fit, the port order as pieces (units that import each other move together), and numbered decisions with a recommended answer: keep units, blocked units, dependencies with no or a partial crate. Then prove the whole program from the outside. `record` and `diff` prove one unit; `app record` and `app replay` prove the app, for CLIs and servers in any of the six languages (the app is a black box): ```sh rust-anything app record . -- python3 cli.py # the command that runs the original rust-anything app replay . # the original must pass 100% rust-anything app replay . --build "target/release/mytool" ``` - `app record` runs the original on the app's own documented examples (`$ mytool ...` lines in its Markdown and shell files, with the files they name), an `--inputs` JSONL file (`{"name", "args", "stdin", "env", "files"}`), and semantic traps derived from those cases (non-ASCII and emoji strings, negative division and modulo, overflow, large and tiny floats, map order, missing files). Each case runs twice; what differs between the two runs becomes a `[..]` wildcard. `--normalize timestamps|uuids|key-order` or `--normalize name=regex` adds normalizers, saved with the cases. - Cases are [trycmd](https://docs.rs/trycmd) files in `rust/app-cases/`: `.toml` (argv, env, exit code), `.stdin`, `.stdout`, `.stderr`, `.in/` (files in) and `.out/` (files written). Read and edit them by hand; a Rust test can run them with `trycmd` once the port has a binary. - `app replay` runs any build against the cases, prints `passed/total`, writes `rust/app-cases/replay-report.md` with a diff per failing case, and exits non-zero on any mismatch. A build that appends to the file named by `RUST_ANYTHING_FALLBACK_LOG` (one line per fallback to the original), as the front door below does, also gets its fallback rate reported. - `app replay --case ` reruns one case by the name the report gives it: the fast, repeatable loop for fixing a mismatch before running everything again. Then move the entry point to Rust and hand it commands one unit at a time: ```sh rust-anything app front-door . # rust/app: every command runs the original rust-anything app wire . textkit --command upper # after textkit-rs passes gate # write the glue in rust/app/src/units/textkit.rs, then: rust-anything app wire . textkit # 100% again, lower fallback rate ``` - `app front-door` scaffolds `rust/app`, a Rust binary named after the app: a clap parser for the commands and flags in the recorded cases, where every command runs the original with the same argv, stdin and environment and passes its output and exit code through. Each fallback is counted, so replaying the fresh front door gives 100% passed at 100% fallback (it builds and replays to show it). It never overwrites `rust/app`: the code is yours from then on. - `app wire --command ` runs `gate` on the unit crate (`--skip-gate` if it just passed), adds it to `rust/app` as a library, writes `src/units/.rs` once for you or your agent to fill in (parse the arguments, call `::port`, print what the original prints), routes the commands to it, then builds and replays. `RUST_ANYTHING_UNIT_=original` sends a wired unit back to the original until the lift. Wire the app's own name as a command (`--command mytool`) for argv that names no command: no arguments, unknown commands, usage errors. When replay passes with fallback rate 0 and every unit passes gate, make it a pure Rust app: ```sh rust-anything app lift . ``` - `app lift` refuses until both hold, and says what blocks it: the cases still falling back, glue still a stub, units failing gate. - On a copy first, it removes the fallback path and the kill switches, turns each unit crate into a plain library of `rust/app` (no `cdylib`, bindings or generated wrappers), and adds `rust/app/tests/app_cases.rs`, which runs `rust/app-cases` with trycmd on `cargo test`, so CI needs nothing but cargo. - Then it runs the lift checklist: fmt, clippy `-D warnings` and tests on every unit and on `rust/app`, every target named in `rust/DECISIONS.md` built or checked where it is installed, files read at run time and asset folders not embedded, and replay on the pure binary. Only when all of it passes are the changes written back. The original is never touched. ### Servers The same commands prove HTTP servers. `--http` says the command starts a server; it takes its port from `PORT` or `{port}` in the command (`--port` for one that always listens on the same port): ```sh rust-anything app record . --http -- node server.js rust-anything app replay . rust-anything app front-door . # axum: every route proxied rust-anything app wire . api --route 'GET /users/{id}' --route '*' rust-anything app lift . ``` - Requests come from `curl` lines in the app's docs (`curl -X POST -d ... http://localhost:8080/x`), `--inputs` (`{"name", "method", "path", "headers", "body"}`) and traps: path segments and query values swapped for the same traps as CLI arguments, bodies for text and JSON traps, and an unknown route. Each run starts the server fresh and sends the requests in name order, so state between requests is kept. - Cases are `rust/app-cases/http/.toml` (the request, the status and the headers that matter) and `.body` (the response body, with `[..]` where two runs differed). Date, server and other per-response headers are left out; delete any header line you do not care about. - The front door is an axum server that starts the original on a port of its own and proxies every route no unit answers. `wire --route` takes axum routes: `METHOD /path/{param}`, `/path` for any method, `*` for everything else; the glue gets the route, its parameters and the request. `lift` removes the proxy; HTTP cases then run in CI with `app replay`. ### Libraries A library has no process to replay: its public API is the front door, and each unit's recorded cases are the proof. ```sh rust-anything app front-door . # rust/app: a Rust crate with the public API # each unit through the loop: bridge, record, port.rs, build, diff, gate; then: rust-anything app wire . textkit-rs # re-exported from rust/app; the original imports its shadow rust-anything app replay . # every wired unit's cases; fallback = exports still in the original rust-anything app lift . ``` - `app front-door` finds the public API (every unit's exports) when the repository has no `main` and no server (`--library` otherwise), and scaffolds `rust/app` as a library crate. Each wired unit becomes a module of it: `pub use textkit_rs::port as textkit;`. - `app wire` takes a crate made by `bridge`, runs `gate`, and writes the unit's shadow drop-in: the original package imports it in place of the unit, so its callers keep the original API and reach the Rust. `RUST_ANYTHING_UNIT_=original` sends the unit back (C: build without the shadow's flags). - `app replay` runs every wired unit's recorded cases through its bindings. The fallback rate is the share of public exports Rust does not answer yet: unwired units, and exports `bridge` keeps in the original language. - `app lift` needs fallback 0 and every unit through `gate`; it strips the bindings, wrappers and shadows from the units and leaves `rust/app` as one pure Rust library. It does not touch any `port.rs`, so the cases that matched through the bindings still describe it; the checklist warns about files of the original that still import the shadows. All five are MCP tools too: `app_record`, `app_replay`, `app_front_door`, `app_wire` and `app_lift`. ## Case study: x18n's core All 29 functions of x18n's core that can move without an API change were ported with rust-anything: every gate passes and 7,925 recorded cases match exactly. `rust-anything bench` then showed the ports are slower than the TS as called from JS, because the bridge costs more than the work. Full report: [`demo/x18n-core`](./demo/x18n-core/README.md). The lesson is built in: measure with `bench` before shipping a port. ## Hot paths: keep the data in Rust A port called once per item pays the bridge once per item, and loses to a JIT. What wins is moving the loop: `profile` finds it, and `--batch` generates a class that takes the items once and runs the function over all of them per call, on all cores, with typed-array results. ```sh rust-anything profile ../x18n -- node --experimental-strip-types $PWD/demo/x18n-search/search.ts . # -> fuzzyScore: a quarter of the run, called per key by `matched`: batch it rust-anything bridge ../x18n packages/core/src/fuzzy.ts --batch fuzzyScore:text ``` ```js const search = new FuzzyScoreBatch(keys) // once const order = search.rank(query, 0) // per keystroke: indexes, best first ``` A `FuzzyScoreIndex` struct in `port.rs` replaces the default loop with one that prepares the items once, and can rank by itself (`rank`): it keeps the keys lowercased with a character mask each, a table of each key's first position of every common character (a one-letter query is one column), and the last query's matches (typing `se` after `s` rescores only what `s` matched). On x18n's sidebar search over 50,000 keys, typed letter by letter, with identical results: | | Per query | vs TS | | --- | ---: | ---: | | TS: `map(fuzzyScore)`, filter, sort | 10 ms | 1x | | TS with the same narrowing as the index | 4.1-5.4 ms | 2x | | The same port, called per key | - | 0.2-0.4x | | `FuzzyScoreBatch`, default index (4 cores) | 5.1 ms | 1.7x | | `FuzzyScoreBatch` with `FuzzyScoreIndex` (napi, 4 cores) | 0.45-0.56 ms | **18-22x** | | The same with wasm (one thread) | 0.95 ms | **11.5x** | Against TS doing the same narrowing, Rust is still 7-12x faster (wasm 5x). Turn the returned indexes into keys with a plain loop: `Array.from(order, i => keys[i])` cost 20x more, 0.4 ms. Every language gets batches, and they beat the original even where per-call ports lose. The same work on 4 cores, identical results and errors (benchmarks in each demo folder): | Language | Workload | Original | Per-call port vs original | Batch vs original | | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | TS | x18n search, 50,000 keys | 10 ms | 0.2-0.4x | **20x** | | Python | `slugify`, 20,000 strings | 98 ms | - | **17x** | | Ruby | `slugify`, 20,000 strings | 110 ms | - | **12.7x** | | Ruby | `shellescape` (stdlib), 50,000 mixed values | 88 ms | - | **11.8x** | | Go | `Slugify`, 50,000 strings | 49 ms | 0.93x | **4x** | | Java | `slugify`, 50,000 strings | 43 ms | 0.68x | **3x** | Compiled originals gain less: the per-item work is already fast, so the batch wins by the number of cores. Batch crates allocate with mimalloc: with the system allocator the Go batch was slower than one thread. Demo: [`demo/x18n-search`](./demo/x18n-search/README.md). ## Real code in six languages Go's `path`, Ruby's `shellwords`, Python's `colorsys`, JDK and glibc behavior behind small facades: every port passes its gate, 13,010 recorded cases in all. The runs found and fixed bugs in rust-anything (floats off by one ULP through `serde_json`, C crashes during recording, untyped code getting garbage inputs). Called per function, the Ruby port runs 4.4x faster than Ruby and the Python port 1.35x faster than CPython, while Go and Java leaf functions stay faster in their own language; as batches, all of them win (see the table above). Report: [`docs/real-world-languages.md`](./docs/real-world-languages.md). ## Example: a real module from x18n `packages/core/src/fuzzy.ts` from [x18n](https://github.com/x18n-dev/x18n), ported both ways in [`demo/`](./demo): ```sh rust-anything analyze ../x18n # fuzzy.ts: ready, wasm-bindgen (core runs in browsers) rust-anything bridge ../x18n packages/core/src/fuzzy.ts --out demo/fuzzy-rs rust-anything record demo/fuzzy-rs --count 2000 # write src/port.rs rust-anything gate demo/fuzzy-rs ``` A first port that indexed by Rust `char` passed simple tests but failed `diff`: ``` 198/200 cases match - fuzzyScore("b😀", "a😀b😀c"): expected {"ok":1997}, got {"ok":1998} ``` JS `indexOf` counts UTF-16 code units, so an emoji is two positions. The port in `demo/*/src/port.rs` uses the generated `utf16` helpers and passes 2000/2000 cases and the gate, as napi-rs (`demo/fuzzy-napi`) and as wasm-bindgen (`demo/fuzzy-rs`). The plan rust-anything writes for all of x18n: [`docs/examples/x18n.md`](./docs/examples/x18n.md). ## Install ```sh cargo install --path . ``` `record`, `diff` and `bench` run the original in its own runtime: Node 22.6+ for TS (it runs `.ts` sources directly), Python 3.9+ for Python and C (ctypes), Go 1.21+, Ruby 3+, JDK 17+ (`javac` and `java`). C also needs a C compiler. wasm bridges also need `rustup target add wasm32-unknown-unknown` and `cargo install wasm-bindgen-cli --version --locked`; `build` names the exact version. For agents, `rust-anything setup` registers everything (see Quick start). To add the MCP server to one project by hand instead (`.mcp.json`): ```json { "mcpServers": { "rust-anything": { "command": "rust-anything", "args": ["mcp"] } } } ``` ## What `bridge` decides - Exports that cannot cross a bridge stay in the source language, with the reason, and the shadow module re-exports the original. For TS: functions that take or return functions, generators and iterators, RegExp, `instanceof` checks, generics, and values whose types (followed through imports, re-exports and `extends`) hold functions. `--keep "name: reason"` keeps more, e.g. code that depends on `Intl` data. - TS types map to Rust types, with type aliases resolved through imports and parameter types inferred from default values; structured values cross as a generated binary wire (JSON only as a fallback for shapes the wire does not model). - JSON cannot express `undefined`, NaN, Infinity, -0 or lone surrogates: structured values carry markers (`{"$undefined": true}`, `{"$num": "NaN"}`, `{"$utf16": [...]}`) that the generated `index.cjs` translates, with helpers in the crate's `js.rs`. `record` runs TS sources as they are: a Node resolve hook follows bundler-style imports (`./errors` to `./errors.ts`), `--resolve-from` supplies npm packages when the repo has none installed, and TS that needs transforming (enums, parameter properties) is retried with `--experimental-transform-types`. ## What `analyze` looks at - Packages (`package.json`) and source files; skips `node_modules`, build output, fixtures, playgrounds, tool configs. items.name: abyssal-garden
items.description: A dreamy underwater world you can swim through in your browser: swaying kelp forests, sunbeams, a sunken ship and manta rays. Everything is generated by code with WebGPU (no images, models or sound files), all in a single 97 KB HTML file.
items.readme:
# Abyssal Garden

**A dreamy underwater world you can swim through, right in your browser.**

Towering kelp forests, sunbeams pouring through a rippling surface, a sunken ship, manta rays gliding overhead.
And all of it is made by code: no images, no 3D models, no sound files. The whole world fits in **one 96 KB HTML file**.

![Kelp forest with a stone whale tail and a manta ray](.github/screenshots/whale-fluke.jpg)

## Try it

1. Download [`index.html`](index.html).
2. Open it in **Chrome** or **Edge** on a desktop computer.
3. Wait a few seconds while the world is built, then press **Dive in** and start swimming.

Nothing to install, and it works offline. It needs a browser with **WebGPU**. If you see *"This scene needs WebGPU"*, update your browser or switch to Chrome / Edge.

## What's down there

- **Kelp forests** that sway in the current and sparkle with tiny gold and green specks
- **Light rays** streaming down from a wavy surface, with shimmering caustics on the sea floor
- **A sunken wooden ship**, a **giant stone whale tail**, rock arches, canyons and floating boulders
- **Manta rays**, schools of fish, rising bubbles and drifting particles
- **A purple grotto** with glowing magenta ground cover, coral and barrel sponges
- **A soundscape** made up as you listen: a deep rumble, distant whale calls, soft chimes and bubbles

| | |
|---|---|
| ![Shipwreck](.github/screenshots/shipwreck.jpg) | ![Looking up through the kelp](.github/screenshots/kelp-forest.jpg) |
| ![Barrel sponges](.github/screenshots/sponge-garden.jpg) | ![Light rays over the kelp basin](.github/screenshots/light-rays.jpg) |

![The purple grotto](.github/screenshots/purple-grotto.jpg)

## Controls

| | Keyboard & mouse |
|---|---|
| Look around | Move the mouse |
| Swim | `W` `A` `S` `D` |
| Up / down | `E` / `Q` |
| Swim faster | Hold `Shift` |
| Jump to a viewpoint | `1` to `6` (the spots in the screenshots) |
| Menu | `Esc` releases the mouse and opens the menu with the list of controls; **Resume** takes you back |
| Sound on / off | `M` (sound starts when you dive in) |
| Performance stats | `H` |
| Detail level | **Low**, **Medium** or **High** in the menu (reloads the page) |

The seabed, cliffs and arches are solid: you glide along the rock instead of swimming into it, and you still fit through every tunnel and arch. Kelp, plants, corals, sponges, loose rocks, the floating boulders, the ship and the whale tail you can swim through.

**On a touchscreen:** hold one finger down to swim forward and slide it to steer. Put a second finger down to go faster. The `≡` button in the corner opens the menu. Phones always show the scene in landscape and start on Low or Medium detail. (Touch support is experimental.)

## Detail levels

The **Low**, **Medium** and **High** buttons in the menu pick the detail level; the current one is lit. Each level is the same world, built with less in it:

| Level | What it is | Picked on a first visit for |
|---|---|---|
| **High** | The full scene | Computers |
| **Medium** | Half of the leaves, sparkles and pebbles; small rocks, sponges and corals cast no shadows | Phones with 8 GB of memory |
| **Low** | A quarter of the leaves, no anti-aliasing, coarser rocks and corals, simpler lighting, 480p to start with | Other phones, and computers with 4 GB of memory or less |

If loading crashes the tab, or the graphics driver gives up, the page starts again one level lower. Your browser remembers the level, and the resolution and draw distance the scene settled on, for the next visit.

## How it works

- The seabed is sculpted on your graphics card every time the page opens, then decorated with about two million kelp leaves and plants, tens of thousands of rocks, and thousands of sponges, corals and fish.
- Everything is drawn with **WebGPU** directly. No game engine or 3D library is used.
- The ship, whale tail, mantas, fish and corals are built from simple mathematical shapes.
- The sound is synthesized live with the Web Audio API.
- It's built to run smoothly: about 180 fps at 2560×1440 on an RTX 5070 Ti. On slower hardware it aims for 60 fps by lowering first the resolution and then how far away plants and rocks are drawn, in small steps. The scene is already running, blurred, behind the start menu, so most of that tuning is done before you dive in. A low-end phone (Samsung Galaxy A16) reaches about 20 fps at 670×372 on Low.

## Make it your own

The readable source code is in the [`source`](source) folder. To change something and rebuild `index.html` you need [Node.js](https://nodejs.org) 18 or newer:

```bash
cd source
npm install
npm run build
```

This writes a new `index.html` next to this README. `npm run build:readable` writes an unminified version instead, which is easier to debug in the browser's developer tools.

`npm run build:dev` writes a separate `dev.html` with two extra tools that are not part of `index.html`: `F` flies the camera along a one-minute path through the whole world, and `B` runs that flight as a benchmark and reports frame and GPU times.

| File | What's inside |
|---|---|
| [`source/src/world.js`](source/src/world.js) | The world layout: rock walls, arches, tunnels, kelp forests, sponge gardens, fish schools, mantas, the ship and the whale tail. **A good place to start.** |
| [`source/src/shaders.js`](source/src/shaders.js) | The look: water and fog colors, lighting, kelp, rocks, the water surface and light rays (WGSL shader code) |
| [`source/src/main.js`](source/src/main.js) | The renderer, the camera, the controls, the six viewpoints and the camera path the world is laid out around |
| [`source/src/audio.js`](source/src/audio.js) | The soundscape |
| [`source/src/quality.js`](source/src/quality.js) | The detail levels: which one a device starts on, and what is remembered between visits |
| [`source/src/math.js`](source/src/math.js) | Noise, random numbers and mesh-building helpers |
| [`source/src/dev.js`](source/src/dev.js) | Development tools (fly-through and benchmark), only in `dev.html` |
| [`source/template.html`](source/template.html) | The page around the scene: loading bar, start menu, links and their styles |

Some easy first tweaks:

- **Water color:** `WCOL` (blue-green water) and `PCOL` (purple grotto) near the top of the shared scene code in `shaders.js`
- **Sunlight color:** `SUNC` right next to them
- **Brightness and light rays:** `EXPO` and `RAYS` in `main.js`
- **Swimming speed:** search for `26 : 7` in `main.js` (fast speed : normal speed)

items.readme:
# Lastbook

Lastbook is an offline survival library for Mac, Windows and Linux. It puts manuals, videos, encyclopedias, an offline map and
short practical guides on one computer. After setup, it works offline. The desktop sidebar opens Videos, Map and Chat.
Chat answers questions using the library and links to its sources.

Website: <https://lastbook.org>. Contact: hello@lastbook.org.

> Lastbook’s original code and documentation are licensed under the [MIT License](LICENSE).
> Contributions are welcome. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) to get started.

## Release status

| Platform | Version | Status |
|---|---|---|
| macOS (Apple Silicon, macOS 14 or later) | 1.1.11 | Live on lastbook.org, signed and notarized |
| Windows (64-bit, Windows 10 or later) | 1.1.11 | Live on lastbook.org, Authenticode signed |
| Linux (Ubuntu 24.04 or 26.04 LTS, x86_64) | 1.1.11 | Ubuntu packages; installation instructions below |

## iPad (development preview, source only)

A native iPad app (Videos, Map and Chat, offline, with optional on-device AI) is in [`mobile/ipad/`](mobile/ipad/).
- It is source for contributors to build and sign themselves.
- There is no App Store, TestFlight or downloadable iPad build.
- See [mobile/ipad/README.md](mobile/ipad/README.md) for what works, the current limitations and how to build it.

## Install on Linux

The Linux packages target **Ubuntu 24.04 LTS and Ubuntu 26.04 LTS on Intel/AMD x86_64 computers**, one package for each. Download
[Lastbook for Ubuntu 24.04](https://downloads.lastbook.org/Lastbook_1.1.11_amd64.deb) (or [for Ubuntu 26.04](https://downloads.lastbook.org/Lastbook_1.1.11_ubuntu26.04_amd64.deb)), then install it with apt so Ubuntu resolves its dependencies.

```bash
sudo apt install ./Lastbook_1.1.11_amd64.deb                  # Ubuntu 24.04
sudo apt install ./Lastbook_1.1.11_ubuntu26.04_amd64.deb      # Ubuntu 26.04
```

Open Lastbook from the application menu. First-run setup downloads your chosen library, state map and optional local AI.
The app uses Ubuntu's GTK, WebKitGTK and media codecs. Its own files install under `/opt/lastbook`, and your library and
settings stay in your home folder. Removing the package leaves those downloaded files and settings in place.

The Linux release was tested on Ubuntu 24.04.5 in WSL2, including installation, setup, video playback, maps, address search,
PDF reading, offline AI with citations, shutdown and uninstall. AI tests used the CPU. Native Linux GPU performance and
other Linux distributions have not been validated for this release.

## What it does

- **Guides first.** Short, curated guides for urgent needs (`content/topics/`), each pointing to real pages in the library
  with page numbers, plus what curators looked for and did not find (`content/gaps.json`).
- **The full library.** Manuals and PDFs (with a whole-PDF view), videos, and offline encyclopedias (ZIM files), with
  keyword search everywhere and meaning-based search on Windows.
- **Offline map.** A base map of the world and the US, plus a detailed map for the state selected during setup: local streets,
  buildings, terrain, crops, and water, help and resource points. Addresses in that state can be found offline. The person
  picks the state; Lastbook never detects location.
- **Optional local AI.** Ask questions in plain words and get answers that cite library pages, from a model that runs on
  the computer itself (see "The local AI" below). Without it, Chat still finds the right pages.
- **One-download setup.** On first run, setup defaults to Small and selects local AI when the computer can run it.
  The person can choose Small, Medium or All, selects a state map, and starts the checked downloads. A library already on the
  computer (a folder or a pack zip) can be used instead of downloading.
- **Check for updates, only when asked.** About has a Check for updates button (and the Mac menu has Lastbook > Check for
  Updates…). It only says whether a newer version is on the website; nothing is downloaded or installed.

## Privacy and network use

- **No listening port.** The desktop app opens no network port. The window and the engine talk through an in-memory bridge
  (`app/bridge.py`): WKURLSchemeHandler on macOS (`app/shell_macos.py`), WebView2 `WebResourceRequested` on Windows
  (`app/shell_windows.py`), and WebKitGTK `URISchemeRequest` on Linux (`app/shell_linux.py`). The local AI runner speaks JSON lines on standard input and output and opens no socket either.
- **Two uses of the network, both started by the person.** (1) Setup's downloader (`engine/setup/`), when the person
  starts or resumes a download. (2) The update check (`engine/update.py`, `web/update.js`), when the person presses
  the button. Both go through `engine/setup/download.py`, the only module that opens a connection: HTTPS on port 443 only,
  to allow-listed hosts only (`downloads.lastbook.org` for packs, maps, the manifest and update information; Hugging Face's
  download hosts for the AI model; the update check accepts `downloads.lastbook.org` alone), no proxy from the system, and a
  redirect is followed only to another allowed host.
- **Pinned trust.** The downloader trusts only the root certificates in `engine/setup/roots.pem` (11 roots from Mozilla's
  bundle), never the system's trust store. The builds refuse to finish if those roots no longer cover the allowed hosts
  (`packaging/check_tls_roots.py`).
- **Checked files.** Every download is checked against the SHA-256 in the manifest before it is used. Zips are checked
  for unsafe paths, links and sizes before anything is written.
- **Nothing else.** The windows block all web loads, there is no telemetry, no account, and nothing runs on a timer or at
  startup that reaches the network.
- **A working library is never broken.** New data is unpacked beside the old one, checked, and then switched in with a
  single rename. A failure at any step leaves the old library as it was.

The setup contract, including state maps, is in [docs/SETUP-API.md](docs/SETUP-API.md); the engine side is described in
[engine/setup/README.md](engine/setup/README.md).

## What's where

| Path | What it is |
|---|---|
| `app/` | The desktop app: entry point (`main.py`), the no-port bridge, the macOS, Windows and Linux shells, and tests (`app/tests/`). |
| `engine/` | Paths and data-folder lookup, library access, saved pages, offline address search (`address_search.py`), the update check (`update.py`) and first-run setup (`engine/setup/`). `engine/vendor-macos/` holds pypdfium2 for the Mac build. |
| `server.py`, `assistant.py`, `retrieval.py`, `llm_local.py` | The engine: request handler, the assistant and its citation checks, keyword plus meaning-based search, and the local AI (model pins, fit check, runner control). |
| `web/` | The interface, in plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript with no build step and nothing loaded from the web. `setup.*` is the setup screen, `update.js` the update check in About. |
| `content/` | The curated guides (`topics/*.json`) and what curators looked for and did not find (`gaps.json`). Format: `content/SCHEMA.md`. |
| `packaging/` | App builds (macOS, Windows and Linux), the Windows installer and its front (`setup_stub/`), signing helper (`sign_windows.ps1`), icons (`icon/`), pack and state-map builders, release manifest, TLS roots tools, package scans, and `packaging/llm/` (the local AI runner). |
| `derived/packs/pack-spec.json` | What goes into each download pack (Small, Medium, All and add-ons) and each state map. Everything else under `derived/` is generated and not kept here. |
| `tools/` | Builders for the offline map, addresses and place finder, plus curator helpers (`libq.py`, `validate_topics.py`). |
| `website/`, `website-next/` | The earlier website and the current static lastbook.org site, respectively. |
| `docs/` | The setup contract (`SETUP-API.md`), how the offline map is put together (`MAPS.md`) and notes on the library server version (`LIBRARY-SERVER.md`). |

## Run from source

You need Python 3.11 or later and a **data folder**. A data folder holds `library-data/catalog.json` (the library) and gets
a `derived/` folder for indexes, caches and logs. Get one by running the app once and letting setup download a pack, or by
unzipping a pack from lastbook.org.

```bash
python3 -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/pip install -r packaging/requirements_macos.txt     # on Windows: packaging/requirements_app.txt
.venv/bin/python app/main.py --data /path/to/LastbookData
```

Without `--data`, the app checks `LASTBOOK_DATA`, the folder chosen last time, and its own data folder.
Existing libraries elsewhere are accessed when the person chooses them. If no library is available, it opens setup.
The full order is in `app/main.py`.

The **library server** version runs the same engine in a browser and can share with phones on the same Wi-Fi:

```bash
LASTBOOK_DATA=/path/to/LastbookData python3 server.py          # then open http://127.0.0.1:8890/
```

See [docs/LIBRARY-SERVER.md](docs/LIBRARY-SERVER.md). It was written for the household library this project grew out of,
so some of its paths and ports describe that setup. The desktop app does not use this port.

## Build the apps

The builds write into `derived/app-build/` and refuse to finish if the package scan finds something that must not ship:
test code, a network call outside setup's downloader, a web address in our own pages, or a word from the private list
(see below). The builds also run the TLS roots gate.

**macOS (Apple Silicon, needs [uv](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv)):**

```bash
bash packaging/llm/build_llm_macos.sh    # optional: the local AI runner, llama.cpp at a pinned tag, Metal
bash packaging/build_app_macos.sh        # Lastbook.app
```

The build uses CPython 3.11.18 exactly (earlier 3.11 releases lack the block on the compromised eMudhra CA keys). It makes
an ad-hoc signed app. Release copies are then signed with the project's Developer ID in a separate release step; its keys
and settings are not in this repository. The build reads the release manifest from a release folder under
`derived/release/`, which is not in this repository either; see `packaging/release_manifest.py`.

**Windows (64-bit, in Git Bash):**

```bash
TOOLS='C:\path\to\tools' bash packaging/llm/build_llm_windows.sh                 # the runner: llama.cpp with Vulkan, CPU fallbacks
PY=/c/path/to/python.exe OUT='C:\path\to\output' bash packaging/build_app_windows.sh
PY=/c/path/to/python.exe DIST='C:\path\to\output\dist\Lastbook' OUT='C:\path\to\output' bash packaging/build_setup_windows.sh
```

`PY` is CPython 3.14.10 or a later 3.14 (python.org's NuGet package) with `packaging/requirements_app.txt` installed. Each
script header lists the tools it needs, with versions and checksums. The three WebView2 files come from the NuGet package
`Microsoft.Web.WebView2` 1.0.3856.49 and are checked against the hashes in `build_app_windows.sh`. libzim is pinned to
3.13.0 on Windows because Smart App Control refuses 3.13.1's `zim-9.dll`.

`build_setup_windows.sh` makes a per-user installer (no administrator prompt). Its front, `packaging/setup_stub/`, is a
small C program with no C runtime that loads DLLs from System32 only. Its payload reader supports the certificate table
and alignment padding appended by Authenticode signing.

To sign during packaging, set `SIGNTOOL`, `SIGNING_DLIB` and `SIGNING_METADATA` to the Windows paths for SignTool,
the Azure Artifact Signing client DLL and your signing metadata file. `build_setup_windows.sh` calls
`packaging/sign_windows.ps1` for the app folder, uninstaller, inner installer and final installer, in that order.
The helper preserves valid vendor signatures and verifies timestamped signatures after signing. Signing credentials
and account metadata stay in the release environment.

The published Windows 1.1.8 installer passed installation and startup checks, and all 90 installed EXE, DLL and PYD files
had valid signatures. The release is 104,960,408 bytes with SHA-256
`0b31eea87fa05523ca710575e5939754fe10a65eb44ee7d88fe975fbbd161d74`.

**Linux (build on Ubuntu 24.04 or 26.04, x86_64)**

```bash
bash packaging/llm/build_llm_linux.sh
bash packaging/linux/build_app_linux.sh
```

The package uses the system Python and pinned wheels from `packaging/linux/requirements_linux.txt`, built for that Python
only, so each Ubuntu release gets its own package. On 24.04 (Python 3.12) the app build creates
`derived/app-build/linux/<timestamp>/Lastbook_1.1.11_amd64.deb`; on 26.04 (Python 3.14) it creates
`Lastbook_1.1.11_ubuntu26.04_amd64.deb`, with the version `1.1.11+ubuntu26.04`, which apt takes as newer than the 24.04 package.
It bundles the local AI runner when `derived/llm/bin-linux/lastbook-llm` exists. `packaging/linux/smoke_deb.sh` checks
the package in a fresh container of the same Ubuntu release.
Linux integration-test helpers live under `app/tests/linux_*`; set `LASTBOOK_TEST_HOST` to a Windows SSH host with WSL2
before running them. Their disposable test distro is named `LastbookTest`, with files under `C:\LastbookTest`.

## Packs, state maps and the local AI

- **Packs** are data folders: a library plus its catalog, search index and map. `packaging/build_packs.py` builds them
  from a frozen snapshot of a full library according to `derived/packs/pack-spec.json`, and `packaging/verify_packs.py` and
  `packaging/scan_pack.py` check them. The published packs are on `downloads.lastbook.org`. Setup downloads the one the
  person picks and checks it against `setup/manifest-v1.json`, which `packaging/release_manifest.py` writes at build time
  (a newer copy is fetched from `downloads.lastbook.org` when setup opens and used only if it validates).
- **State maps** are one US state's detailed map set, built by `packaging/build_packs.py map <ST>` and published by
  `packaging/state_maps.py`, with per-state address indexes from `packaging/address_indexes.py`. A state map replaces the
  library's map set; it never merges with it. Medium already holds California and All the whole US.
- **The local AI** is optional: Gemma 4 26B A4B (Unsloth's `gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-UD-Q4_K_M.gguf`, about 17 GB). The file
  name, size, SHA-256 and Hugging Face revision are pinned in `llm_local.py`. Setup offers it only where the measured fit
  says it fits (about 18 GB of memory for model and context, plus a reserve) and says why in plain words when it does not.
  Setup downloads it directly from Hugging Face. The model is never part of the app or of this repository. The runner,
  `lastbook-llm`, is our own small program (`packaging/llm/lastbook_llm.cpp`) on llama.cpp tag b12032: Metal on a Mac,
  Vulkan with CPU fallbacks on Windows and Linux.
- **Meaning-based search** uses BAAI's bge-small-en-v1.5 (ONNX) through onnxruntime, on Windows only; the Mac build uses
  keyword search.

## What is not in this repository, and why

- **The library** (`library-data/`): hundreds of gigabytes of third-party manuals, videos and encyclopedias, each under
  its own terms. It is distributed as packs, with a Sources and permissions page in each pack.
- **Models and maps** (GGUF, ONNX, map data): large, and published by their makers or built from public data. Setup
  fetches them, and the checksums and pins are here.
- **Generated data** (`derived/`, builds, installers): everything there can be rebuilt with the scripts here.
- **Release and signing material**: signing keys and certificates, notarization and Azure settings, deploy settings and
  the release folders.
- **Private data**: the household's own home area (`web/home-area.json`), the private word lists the scans use, machine
  and user names, keys and internal security-audit notes. The guides here are already in their shipped, general wording.
  To keep your own home-area words out of a build, put them in a local copy of `packaging/ship_edits.json` (`forbidden`)
  and never commit it.

## Tests

```bash
python3 -B -m unittest app.tests.test_bridge app.tests.test_setup app.tests.test_data_folder app.tests.test_what_ships app.tests.test_update app.tests.test_address_search app.tests.test_topic_search app.tests.test_chat_steps app.tests.test_validate_topics app.tests.test_libq
```

`test_bridge` needs a data folder (`LASTBOOK_DATA`); the others run without a library. `packaging/test_pack_tools.py SAMPLE
WORK` checks the pack tools against a pack sample (`build_packs.py build <pack> --sample N`). The `mac_*` and `win_*`
scripts in `app/tests/` drive a real build against a real data folder, and their paths are placeholders
(`/path/to/lastbook`, `C:\Users\you\app-test`) to set for your own machine.

## Contributing and licence

See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) and [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md). Lastbook’s original code and
documentation use the [MIT License](LICENSE), permitting commercial use, modification and redistribution with the
copyright and license notice. Third-party software, models, media and library content retain their own licenses,
listed in [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md) and each library pack. Distributed app bundles include
GPL-covered components such as python-libzim and libzim and must also meet those components’ license obligations.

## Website maintenance

`website-next/` is the deployed site. Run `python3 -I tools/build.py` from that folder to rebuild the main pages.
The current emergency buying guide is maintained directly in `buying-guide/index.html` and `buying-guide.css`,
with image provenance in `buying-guide/IMAGE-SOURCES.md`. The older `tools/buying_guide.py` and
`data/buying-guide.json` describe the preceding guide and will overwrite the current guide if run.
The current guide contains 17 named products with matching photos. Deployment-specific Amazon Associates tags
are omitted from this repository.

items.readme:
# muse.ai 注册 / 邀请码兑换 协议分析

补充一下，记得用JP 节点， JP 不需要绑卡，直接过

纯 HTTP 实现 muse.ai 的注册与邀请码兑换流程，不依赖浏览器。本文记录的是通过抓包逐字段比对得出的协议细节。

## 快速开始

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
cp config.example.json config.json   # 填入邮箱与可选代理
python example_register.py
```

## 目录结构

```
musepy/
  client.py    注册 + 兑换的完整协议客户端
  runner.py    多账号批量调度（sticky 代理 / 预算 / 停止语义）
  otp.py       验证码轮询（幂等：只取 send 之后的最新码）
  falco.py     行为埋点上报（可选）
  caa.py       注册漏斗事件上报（可选）
example_register.py        单账号端到端示例
example_batch.py           多账号批量示例
config.example.json        配置模板
test_onboarding_smoke.py   离线冒烟（披露解析纯函数）
test_runner_smoke.py       离线冒烟（批量调度，mock 网络）
```

## 协议流程

```
GET  /                                   拿初始 cookie
POST /api/auth/native/restart            → 201 {csrf_token}
POST /api/auth/native/send-otp           → 201
POST /api/auth/native/confirm-otp        → 200 {registration_state:"completion_required",
                                               tos:{content_version}}（动态 TOS 版本）
POST /api/auth/native/register-completion→ 200 {auth_meta_session:{frl_access_token, frl_account_id}}
POST auth.meta.com/hatch/session/bootstrap/ → 302…→ muse.ai 200 HTML（会话引导，必须）
     └ 从 muse.ai 文档解析动态披露 disclosure_text/disclosure_version 与状态门
       （resolvedDestination/isGeoGated/waitlist → 地区受限）
POST /api/hatch/accept-tos               → 200（单次调用；正文用服务端动态披露，非硬编码）
GET  /api/hatch/invite                   → 200 表示账号有效
POST /api/hatch/vm/wake                  → 200（必须，否则兑换误报 invalid；
                                             wake_trigger=mount + open_id + away_ms=0）
POST /api/hatch/stateful-sharing         → 200
POST /api/hatch/invite-code/redeem       → 200 {redemptionStatus:"redeemed"}
POST /api/hatch/invite                   → 200 {code}（取回自己的码，不等于页面刮开 reveal）
```

## 几个容易踩的坑

### 1. `confirm-otp` 必须带 `supports_muse_link_transparency: true`

```json
{"otp_code":"123456","remember_device":true,"supports_muse_link_transparency":true}
```

### 2. `register-completion` 的姓名字段语义

```json
{
  "date_of_birth": "1993-11-14",
  "first_name": "三郎",     // 名（given name）
  "last_name": "近藤",      // 姓（family name）
  "tos_content_version": "ntm_create_account:default_v1_meta_account_v3+docs_v2",
  "remember_device": true
}
```

`first_name` 是名、`last_name` 是姓，与直觉相反。生日早于约 18 年前会返回 403——同一会话同一份姓名，只把生日从 2013 改成 1993 就能从 403 变 200。

### 3. `restart` 的 body 不是空对象

```json
{"resume": false}
```

### 4. `accept-tos` 是会话激活开关，且必须先引导会话

注册完成后**必须先走 `POST auth.meta.com/hatch/session/bootstrap/`**（form 表单只带
`frl_access_token`，手动跟随 302/301/303 跳转落到 muse.ai 200 文档），否则后续
hatch 接口一律 403。引导落地的 muse.ai 文档里带有 Next Flight 序列化的动态披露
（`disclosureText` / `disclosureVersion`，当前实测版本为 `HATCH_ROW_v0`），`accept-tos`
的正文必须用服务端返回的这份动态文案（**不是**硬编码常量），`Referer` 用披露页
URL；单次调用即可，不重试，403 时把响应体前 200 字符带出来便于诊断。

引导后若服务端判定 `resolvedDestination == "waitlist"` 或 `isGeoGated == true`，
属于**地区受限**：注册已完成、账号保留，但未证明已加入名单。

### 5. `vm/wake` 缺失会让兑换误报

不调 `vm/wake` 直接兑换，即使是有效码也会返回：

```json
{"success":false,"reason":"invalid","detail":"この招待コードは存在しません"}
```

需要先从已登录页面提取 `vmId`：

```python
re.search(r'vmId[\\"]*:[\\"]*([0-9a-fA-F-]{36})', html)
```

`wake` 的 body 实测为：`wake_trigger: "mount"`（首连）、`open_id`（新 uuid）、
`away_ms: 0`，而不是早期的 `resume`。

### 6. 兑换失败原因的含义

| reason | 含义 |
|---|---|
| `redeemed` | 成功 |
| `already_redeemed` | 本账号已经兑换过一个码 |
| `used_up` | 该码达到 30 次使用上限 |
| `invalid` | 码不存在，或没调 `vm/wake` |

## Cookie

注册成功后 `hatch_sess` 由 `register-completion` 的响应头下发（约 886 字符），这是后续所有 hatch 接口的凭证。`hatch_vml` 在注册阶段一直是被清空状态（`Max-Age=0`），不属于必需项。

## 多账号批量（musepy/runner.py）

```bash
python example_batch.py [count]
```

`config.json` 里的批量字段：

| 字段 | 说明 |
|---|---|
| `otp_file` | 邮箱清单，每行 `email----otp源URL`（otp 源返回 `[{"otp","time"},...]` JSON） |
| `proxy_file` | sticky 代理池，每行 `host:port:user:pass`（或 `host:port`） |
| `codes_file` | 可选，待兑换邀请码池，每行一个 |
| `output_dir` / `tried_file` | 每账号结果 JSON 目录 / 已尝试邮箱清单 |
| `workers` / `max_per_ip` | worker 数（默认 5）/ 每条代理的验证成功上限（默认 6） |
| `resolve_ip` | 是否通过 ipify 解析出口 IP（默认 true） |
| `send_caa` | 批量模式下是否上报注册漏斗埋点 |

调度语义（与本地实现一致，不承诺任何绕过行为）：

- **worker 独占 sticky 代理**：一条代理行同一时刻只归一个 worker（claim/release），
  不抢他人的行；代理池耗尽才共享并打日志。
- **max_per_ip 按验证成功数计**：达到上限释放当前行并换另一行，原行本轮避开。
- **pre-send 传输失败重试**：`bootstrap`/`restart` 等**未发出 OTP 前**的网络失败，
  释放当前代理并**同邮箱换代理重试，上限 3 次**，不消耗新邮箱；仍失败标记 tried。
- **业务拒绝 / pending / 已发 OTP 后的失败：整批停止**——不换行、不重试、不补号。
- **region_waitlist**：账号已注册但地区受限——记录 `registered_waitlist`、账号保留，
  整批停止。
- **预算 = 领取的不同邮箱数**：失败不补号；结束打印 batch_summary JSON
  （queued/started/remaining/ok/pending/server_rejected/transport_error/failed/
  ip_switches/stopped/stop_reason）。

每账号结果写入 `output_dir/<email>.json`，字段：`email/status/stage/registered/
own_code/own_code_status/reveal_status/is_revealed/ip/last_error`。
`frl_access_token` 与 `hatch_sess` 仅在内存中使用，**不落盘**。

OTP 轮询幂等：每次 `send_otp` 前记录开始时间，`musepy/otp.py` 只取该时间之后的
最新 6 位验证码（45 秒超时、0.6 秒间隔、单请求 15 秒超时）。

## 埋点说明

站点前端会上报两类遥测：

- **falco**（`POST /api/falco`）—— 性能指标与业务交互事件，`machineId` 固定为 `not_set`
- **caa-events**（`POST /api/auth/caa-events`）—— 注册漏斗，通过 `navigator.sendBeacon` 逐步骤上报，同一 `waterfall_id` 贯穿全程

两者都不参与注册判定，缺省不影响流程能跑通。`musepy/falco.py` 与 `musepy/caa.py` 保留了完整实现，可通过配置关闭。

## 使用声明

本项目仅供个人、非商业的学习与研究使用，不采用 MIT 等开源许可证。不得用于商业用途或再分发。实际使用时请遵守目标站点的服务条款与当地法律法规。

六大内容形态分流 · 27 类分频道目录 · 统一屏蔽词省额度 · AI 语义定级 · 多路由精准推送

简体中文 · English

多路由精准推送」** 把每条内容送到它该去的位置： - 只想纯粹蹲羊毛？首页默认 **「真福利精选」** 严格锁定 AI 验真的 `freebie`（直接白嫖 + 实操可领的有条件福利），绝不被付费好价、拼车、二手或新闻污染。 - 想看 **黑五 VPS 好价 / 合规拼车 / 开源项目 / 重大新闻与科技资讯**？一键切换顶部兴趣频道即可浏览各自专属的下级分类、真实有效计数与图文卡片，并可分别配置互不干扰的 Telegram 专题推送路由。 --- > 在线演示： --- ## 界面预览 | 工作台列表视图（多兴趣频道栏 + 跨源折叠 + 兑换码一键复制） | 三列图文卡片视图（零额外请求封面图提取 + 响应式 2列/3列网格） | | :---: | :---: | | ![工作台列表视图](docs/ui-public.png) | ![三列图文卡片视图](docs/ui-grid.png) | | 多路由精准推送（分形态/分类/获取方式/关键词定制即时或攒批路由） | AI 语义引擎（27 类分流、自适应学习与零 Token 存量重整分类） | | :---: | :---: | | ![多路由精准推送](docs/ui-push-panel.png) | ![AI 语义引擎](docs/ui-ai-panel.png) | --- ## 核心特性 ### 1. 多兴趣频道与「形态 × 领域 × 获取方式」正交分类 - **6 大内容形态（`kind`）**：`freebie`（白嫖福利）、`deal`（特价好价·含黑五 额度）、`vps`（VPS/主机）、`cloud`（云服务）、`domain`（域名/建站）、`opensource`（开源软件）、`software`（软件授权）、`dev`（开发/工程）、`design`（设计/素材）、`security`（安全/网络）、`hardware`（硬件/数码）、`media`（影音会员）、`game`（游戏）、`carpool`（拼车/合租）、`trade`（二手/交易）、`headline`（时政要闻）、`world`（国际要闻）、`finance`（经济/商业）、`stock`（股票/市场）、`tech`（科技动态）、`news`（综合资讯）、`goods`（实物/优惠）、`offline`（实物福利）、`invite`（邀请码）、`edu`（教育/考试）、`pan`（网盘资源）、`course`（网课/教程）、`other`（其它）。 - **8 个兴趣频道与自适应下级分类**：真福利、全部白嫖、实物福利、网盘/网课、好价、开源、重要新闻、行业资讯； - 「真福利 / 全部白嫖」只展现福利类目（隐藏拼车/交易/新闻要闻，网盘/网课/实物福利各自独立成频道），统计数字实时排除 `noise` 假数； - 「重要新闻 / 行业资讯」自动切换为资讯栏目视角（时政要闻、国际要闻、经济/商业、股票/市场、科技前沿、AI 前沿、开发工程、开源生态、安全/漏洞、硬件数码、综合资讯）； - 切换频道自动重置不兼容的形态、获取方式与价格上限，避免空屏串态。 - **6 级获取方式（`obtain`）**：严格区分 `free`（直接白嫖）、`conditional`（有条件）、`lottery`（抽奖）、`trial`（试用/Demo）、`promo`（推广/引流）、`paid`（需付费）。 ### 2. 三层高信噪比治理（统一屏蔽 · AI 定级 · 零 Token 重整） - **统一屏蔽词防火墙（省额度 + 隐网页 + 拦推送）**：在「订阅与屏蔽」配置关键词、正则或分源规则，不仅隐藏网页条目、拦截推送与日报，**在采集入库送 AI 审核及历史补审前也会直接跳过**，无需在两处重复配置。 - **AI 语义审核引擎**：支持任意 OpenAI 兼容接口，单次输出 `keep`、`kind`、`category`、`obtain`、`quality`（1–5 星）与中文理由；支持白嫖专源免审直通、追加补充规则、从收藏/关闭自动学习个人偏好。 - **零 Token 存量分类重整**：内置「重整分类 (0 Token)」入口与 CLI，更新关键词规则后可一键将历史 `other` 条目零成本归位到细分类目。 ### 3. 三种响应式视图与零请求封面图提取 - **单行紧凑 / 2列卡片 / 3列卡片** 一键切换并记住偏好。 - 14 路采集器（Epic / Steam / GamerPower / CheapShark / GOG / RSS `` & `` / Telegram / LINUX DO / V2EX / B站 / 微博 / CCTV / Bluesky / 本地回环）零额外请求提取封面图，纯文本条目自动收起封面区避免网格空洞。 ### 4. 多路由精准 Telegram 推送 - **全局策略 + 多专题路由**：支持一键新增或可视化编辑独立路由（例如：「🎁 真福利直推」「🖥 黑五/VPS 即时提醒」「📦 开源项目攒批汇总」「📰 新闻资讯早报」），每条路由可单独设定形态、分类、获取方式、关键词、最高价、最低分、即时/攒批模式与自定义前缀头。 - **推送时机与兜底**：支持「推送前先过 AI（防误推）」与「极速抢码先推后审（后台补审后自动补推）」；提供 `strict` / `rule_fallback` / `ignore_ai` 三种 AI 兜底模式。 - **防误推二次校验与诊断预览**：攒批发送前二次回查 DB 状态与最新屏蔽词；支持查看拦截原因分布与路由命中预览；内置夜间静默时段与多语言/时效闸门。 ### 5. 极简部署与单密码鉴权分区 - **零外部数据库**：基于 `node:24-alpine` 原生运行 TypeScript，内置 `node:sqlite`（WAL 模式 + 内存上限调优，自动增量迁移至 Schema v30），日常运行内存 < 100MB。 - **111 个内置数据源（默认精选启用 62 个）**：覆盖 LINUX DO、NodeSeek（含福利/资讯/拼车交易板块）、V2EX、NGA（优惠/拼车/二手）、B站、微博、CCTV 新闻、OpenRouter `:free` 模型、GitHub、Epic、Steam、GamerPower、CheapShark、ITAD、SharewareOnSale、TickCoupon、Reddit、Bluesky、Telegram 频道与中文主机圈促销博客，并支持自定义 RSS 与本地回环/油猴脚本抓取知乎/小红书/小黑盒。 - **公开/管理隔离**：配置 `ADMIN_TOKEN` 后，资源流与每日精选保持公开浏览，管理配置与写入接口全部自动鉴权保护。 - **可选的公开多用户模式**：设 `SITE_MODE=public` + LINUX DO OAuth 后，公共内容仍只读共享，但「不想看 / 收藏 / 已读 / 屏蔽词 / 关注词」按登录用户隔离；未登录访客的偏好只存本机浏览器；登录用户可绑自己的 Telegram Bot 收个人推送，也能订阅公开 RSS 或个人专属 RSS。管理权限始终只认 `ADMIN_TOKEN`，OAuth 登录不会提权。详见 [docs/accounts.md](docs/accounts.md)。 --- ## 工作流架构 ```mermaid flowchart LR S["111 个内置源 + 自定义 RSS + 回环/油猴"] --> E["规则初筛与特征抽取（14 路封面图 / 兑换码 / 价格 / 双语去重指纹）"] E --> F{"统一屏蔽与噪音初筛（block_rules + NOISE_TITLE）"} F -->|命中屏蔽/硬噪音| D["跳过 AI 省额度并隔离"] F -->|通过| M{"AI 审核分流"} M -->|白嫖专源免审| A1["直标 freebie · 进精选"] M -->|AI 语义定级| Q["输出 keep · kind · category · obtain · quality"] Q -->|freebie / deal / opensource / info| P["Web 多频道工作台（紧凑 / 2列 / 3列）"] Q -->|命中多路由规则| R["Telegram 多专题路由（即时直推 / 定时攒批 / 每日精选）"] ``` --- ## 快速开始（开箱即用） ### 方式一：Docker Compose（推荐，1 分钟跑起来） 不需要预先安装 Node.js 或手动建表，**甚至不复制 `.env` 也可以直接启动**： ```bash git clone https://github.com/ZiChuanLan/freebie-radar.git cd freebie-radar # 可选：复制并编辑环境变量（设置 ADMIN_TOKEN 管理密码、Telegram 推送、AI 等） cp .env.example .env # 启动服务（默认监听 http://127.0.0.1:8788） docker compose up -d --build ``` > **需要采集带 Cloudflare 护盾的站点（如 LINUX DO）？** > 仓库已内置可选 `cf` profile，一条命令同时拉起 FlareSolverr： > ```bash > # 在 .env 中设置 FLARESOLVERR_URL=http://flaresolverr:8191 > docker compose --profile cf up -d --build > ``` 验证健康状态与日志： ```bash curl http://127.0.0.1:8788/health # {"ok":true,"version":"0.1.0",...} docker compose logs -f --tail 50 ``` 数据库保存在 `./data/radar.db`，升级只需 `git pull && docker compose up -d --build`，自动完成数据库迁移，数据零丢失。 ### 方式二：源码运行（Node.js ≥ 22.5 + pnpm 10） ```bash git clone https://github.com/ZiChuanLan/freebie-radar.git cd freebie-radar pnpm install cp .env.example .env # 按需填写 ADMIN_TOKEN / 代理 / Telegram 等 pnpm build # 构建前端产物到 dist/web pnpm start # 自动建表迁移 + 初始化 111 个数据源 + 启动 :8788 ``` 开发模式（前后端热更新）： ```bash pnpm dev # 后端 API :8788 pnpm dev:web # 前端 Vite :5173（自动代理 /api 到 8788） ``` --- ## 环境变量说明（`.env`） 所有策略配置（AI 模型/提示词/初筛开关、多路由推送/静默时段、屏蔽词、数据源启停与周期、数据保留天数）均**在网页管理区实时热修改**，`.env` 仅需关注进程级环境变量： | 变量名 | 默认值 | 说明 | |---|---|---| | `PORT` / `HOST` | `8788` / `0.0.0.0` | HTTP 监听端口与地址 | | `DATABASE_PATH` | `./data/radar.db` | SQLite 路径（Docker 内固定 `/data/radar.db`） | | `ADMIN_TOKEN` | 留空（开放） | 管理区密码；**部署到公网强烈建议设置强密码** | | `FLARESOLVERR_URL` | 留空 | FlareSolverr 地址，如 `http://flaresolverr:8191` | | `HTTP_PROXY` / `HTTPS_PROXY` | 留空 | 采集出口代理（海外服务器可留空） | | `PUSH_CHANNEL` | `none` | 设为 `telegram` 启用推送 | | `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` | 留空 | Telegram Bot Token（`@BotFather` 获取） | | `TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID` | 留空 | 接收推送的个人/群组 Chat ID | | `TELEGRAM_PROXY` | 留空 | 仅用于 Telegram 推送的代理 | | `AI_BASE_URL` / `AI_API_KEY` / `AI_MODEL` | 留空 | 首次启动默认 AI 参数，之后推荐在网页「AI 引擎」修改 | | `INGEST_TOKEN` | 留空（禁止写入） | 给 `scripts/pw-collect.mjs` 或油猴脚本回传数据的 Bearer Token | | `GITHUB_TOKEN` | 留空 | 可选，将 GitHub 采集限额从 60/h 提升到 5000/h | | `ENABLE_SCHEDULER` | `true` | 是否开启内置采集、攒批、每日精选与清理调度 | | `DAILY_CRON` / `DAILY_TOP_N` | `30 8 * * *` / `12` | 每日精选生成时间与条数 | --- ## 登录态站点采集（知乎 / 小红书 / 小黑盒） 这三个站点依赖浏览器登录态与前端签名，通过 `scripts/pw-collect.mjs` 使用持久化 Chrome Profile 运行，支持本机或带图形桌面的远程服务器： - **本机回环登录服务（推荐）**：运行 `node scripts/pw-collect.mjs serve`，在网页「数据源运维」点「扫码登录」打开登录窗口扫码，登完自动抓取公开帖并回传雷达。也支持直接复制页面提供的 **Tampermonkey 油猴脚本**，无需本地安装 Node/Playwright。 - **服务器定时脚本**： ```bash PROFILE_DIR=/data/profile SERVER_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8788 HEADLESS=1 INGEST_TOKEN=your_token node scripts/pw-collect.mjs ``` - **隐私边界**：服务端不保存任何 Cookie 或账号凭据，登录态仅留存在本地 `PROFILE_DIR`。 --- ## 常用 CLI 工具 ```bash pnpm tsx src/server/cli.ts sources # 查看全部 111 个数据源与最近运行状态 pnpm tsx src/server/cli.ts collect [sourceId] # 立即采集（不传则跑全部启用源） pnpm tsx src/server/cli.ts enable # 启用指定源 pnpm tsx src/server/cli.ts disable # 禁用指定源 pnpm tsx src/server/cli.ts config # 更新指定源配置 pnpm tsx src/server/cli.ts reclassify # 重跑规则分类、评分与双语去重键 pnpm tsx src/server/cli.ts ai-review [limit] # 批量补审未审条目 pnpm tsx src/server/cli.ts daily [--dry-run] # 生成或预览每日精选 pnpm tsx src/server/cli.ts digests # 查看历史每日精选日期 pnpm tsx src/server/cli.ts stats # 查看分类统计 pnpm tsx src/server/cli.ts diagnose # 推送筛选与命中体检 pnpm tsx src/server/cli.ts obtain # 按获取方式重算统计 ``` --- ## 目录结构与延伸文档 ```text src/ ├── server/ │ ├── collectors/ # 采集器与调度（SEEDS / dispatchFresh / 封面图提取） │ ├── enrich/ # 归一化、双语去重、27 类规则、形态分流(kind)、获取方式(obtain)、AI 队列与屏蔽词 │ ├── push.ts # 多路由分流、Telegram 即时/攒批二次校验、静默时段、预览诊断 │ ├── digest.ts # 每日精选生成与格式化 │ ├── retention.ts # 数据保留策略与自动清理 │ ├── ai-admin.ts # AI 管理、历史补审与零 Token 存量重分类 │ └── routes.ts # Hono REST API 与单密码鉴权分区 └── web/ # React 19 + Vite + Tailwind v4 工作台（紧凑 / 2列 / 3列视图 + 多路由编辑器） ``` 延伸文档见 `docs/`： - [`docs/data-sources.md`](docs/data-sources.md) — 数据源清单与可达性说明 - [`docs/obtain.md`](docs/obtain.md) — 获取方式（`free` / `conditional` / `lottery` / `trial` / `promo` / `paid`）分级体系 - [`docs/ai.md`](docs/ai.md) — AI 语义审核口径与误判治理 - [`docs/push.md`](docs/push.md) — 推送分级分流、去重与静默时段 - [`CHANGELOG.md`](CHANGELOG.md) — 版本变更记录 --- ## 免责与许可 - 本项目仅对公开网页与接口信息进行聚合、筛选与去重，不存储或传播受版权保护的内容，不提供账号共享；请遵守各目标站点的服务条款并控制合理抓取频率。 - 基于 [MIT License](LICENSE) 开源。如果这个项目帮到了你，欢迎点个 ⭐ Star 支持！ - 致谢 [LinuxDo](https://linux.do) 以及所有反馈问题、补充源适配与参与改进的开发者。
