items.description: 麦田：自媒体多平台发布中控与数据监控（B站/抖音/小红书/视频号/YouTube/X），飞书卡片通知 + 数据大屏
items.readme:
一行装好 · 看它跑一遍 · 怎么配合 · 各平台的坑 · 作者

一个人做内容，要发六七个平台，每个平台的文案、封面、发布形式都不一样；发完还想知道哪期起来了、哪个平台涨粉、哪个平台真的带来了付费。麦田就是我自己每天在用的那套工作台： 1. **发得出去**：一期视频分批填好 B站、抖音、小红书、视频号、YouTube、X、Instagram，提前排进「分发计划」，到点发布、自动取链接。 2. **看得清楚**：每期在每个平台的播放、互动，各平台粉丝，每天自动采、长期留存；手机上看大屏，飞书群推卡片。 3. **算得出钱**：接上你自己的站点，看哪一期、哪个平台带来了注册和收入。 > 跑在一台常开的 Mac 上，用你自己登录好的浏览器操作各平台，**不存任何平台密码**。国内四家只填写不发布，最后一下由你自己点。 ## 看它跑一遍

一期视频从写文案到上线（47 秒，各平台发布页为示意，数据是作者第 4 期的真实文案和封面）· 高清 MP4

大屏（演示数据，node src/demo.mjs 就能看到）

| 日历：分发计划 | 单期复盘：同龄对比 | 每期转化漏斗 | |---|---|---| | | | | ## 怎么配合

| 部分 | 做什么 | 在哪 | |---|---|---| | 发布 skill | 让 AI 助手（Claude Code / Codex）看片、写各平台文案、生成发布工程并校验 | 本仓库 [`skills/maitian-publish`](skills/maitian-publish/SKILL.md) | | 麦田发布助手 | Chrome 插件，各平台适配器：打开上传页、传视频和封面、填文案、设定时 | [Chrome 应用商店](https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/eaaipbilkhibicihiollecmbpneikpnj)（装进麦田的专用 Chrome，自动更新） | | 麦田（本仓库） | 分发计划、调度、防重、等你点发布、取链接、采数据、网页大屏、飞书通知 | 本仓库 | 链路：成片 → skill 写「发布素材.md」→ 生成 `publish.json` → `hub plan` 进分发计划 → `hub run` 分批填写 → 国内平台你点发布 → 到点取链接 → 每天采数据 → 大屏和飞书卡片。 ## 一行装好 ```bash bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CzzzzzzJ/mdldm-maitian/main/scripts/install.sh)" ``` 下载麦田和发布助手到 `~/maitian/`、接上发布 skill、打开安装向导；向导问完几个问题，生成配置、装好开机自启、打开各平台登录页。需要 macOS、Node.js ≥ 22.5、Google Chrome。 Windows（社区贡献，感谢 [ajin558](https://github.com/ajin558)；开机自启暂未适配）： ```powershell powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Command "irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CzzzzzzJ/mdldm-maitian/main/scripts/install-windows.ps1 | iex" ``` 同样下载到 `%USERPROFILE%\maitian\`、接上发布 skill、打开安装向导，安装目录里另有 4 个双击启动器（演示 / 登录 / 体检 / 启动）。需要 Windows 10/11、Node.js ≥ 22.5、Google Chrome；缺 Git / Node 时脚本会用 winget 自动补装。开机自启暂未适配（向导里的 launchd 步骤会自动跳过），可用任务计划程序指向安装目录的 `4-start.bat` 代替。

手动安装 或者手动： 需要：macOS、Node.js ≥ 22.5（用到内置 `node:sqlite`）、Google Chrome；可选 NAS（放成片）、飞书群机器人、cloudflared。 ```bash git clone https://github.com/CzzzzzzJ/mdldm-maitian.git && cd mdldm-maitian node src/demo.mjs # 先用假数据看看效果：http://localhost:8788/?key=demo node src/init.mjs # 安装向导：检查环境、生成 config.json、装开机自启；在专用 Chrome 里从应用商店添加麦田发布助手、登录各平台 node src/hub.mjs doctor # 登录完检查各平台登录态和上传页（不上传、不填写） ``` 打开向导最后给出的地址（`http://localhost:8787/?key=`），之后浏览器会记住口令。手动安装也可以：`cp config.example.json config.json` 填好后跑 `scripts/install-launchd.sh`。
### 三级上手 | 级别 | 你能得到 | 要装的 | 大概时间 | |---|---|---|---| | L1 只看数据 | 各平台粉丝、已发作品的播放互动、大屏、飞书日报 | 麦田；专用 Chrome 里登录各平台；已发的期用 `hub adopt` 登记 | 30 分钟 | | L2 分发 | 一期一次填好七个平台，定时，自动取链接 | + [麦田发布助手](https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/eaaipbilkhibicihiollecmbpneikpnj)（应用商店装进专用 Chrome）；+ 发布 skill（或手写 `publish.json`） | 再 1 小时 | | L3 转化 | 每期带来的注册和收入 | + 你自己的站点按 `src/site.mjs` 的接口接入 | 看站点 | ## 它做什么 - **播种（发布）**：读 NAS 上的一期发布工程（成片、封面、各平台文案、定时），按批次在专用 Chrome 里填好各平台上传页。 - X、YouTube、Instagram、自有站点：回读文案和定时一致后自动提交，只点一次。 - B站、抖音、小红书、视频号：**填好就停**，等你自己点「发布 / 定时发布」，守护进程每 20 分钟提醒。 - 防重：库里已经到位的平台不再跑；X 定时列表、YouTube Studio、Instagram 主页、站点后台已有同名的不再传。 - **长势（流量和粉丝）**：每天上午采一次各期在各平台的播放和互动、各平台粉丝数；新一期头三天每 6 小时采一次。 - **收成（转化，可选）**：接上自有站点后，看注册、会员、订单、收入从哪个渠道、哪一期来。 - **日历**：上周到未来两周，已发布、已定时、等你点、计划中的期一眼看清。 - **粮仓（档案）**：每期的封面、文案快照、各平台链接、过程日志。 - **复盘（数据分析）**：每期发布后第 1/3/7 天自动出复盘卡片：各平台占比、互动率、和上一期同龄对比（第 N 天对第 N 天）、期间涨粉、带来的注册；每周一出周报。网页单期页有同一份复盘表，转化页有每期转化漏斗（播放 → 注册 → 会员 → 收入）。 - **飞书通知**：开跑、每个平台到位、异常、等你点发布、定时被平台改掉、每日日报、复盘和周报，都是带颜色的卡片。 ## 各平台的坑（实战总结） - **国内四家由你自己点最终发布**。自动化只负责填写和核对，最后一下人点，降低风控风险。 - **小红书只走最保守的路**：只读页面上已经渲染的内容、像人一样滚动和点击，不在页面里直接调它的接口，低频。 - **同一条视频每个平台只上传一次**，反复重传最容易触发风控；中控的防重就是为这个。 - **视频号的定时可能被改**：表单回读是对的，提交后平台记成别的时间（遇到过 +2 小时）。`sync` 会拿平台记录的定时和计划比对，不一致发 ⚠️ 卡片。 - **YouTube 上传对话框被关掉**时，视频可能已经排好定时；中控会先查 Studio 列表再下结论。 - **成片必须 faststart**（moov 在文件头），否则小红书报「无视频流信息」、抖音不出表单；校验会拦。 - **专用 Chrome 卡死**：用 `curl 127.0.0.1:9333/json/close/` 关掉卡住的标签页，不会触发「离开此网站」确认。
架构 ``` ┌────────────── Mac（常开）──────────────┐ NAS 发布工程 │ hub.mjs 守护进程 ──── 专用 Chrome（CDP 9333）── 各平台创作者后台 publish.json ─▶│ │ ▲ ▲ │ 成片/封面 │ │ │ 平台适配器（麦田发布助手 lib/） │ │ ▼ │ │ │ SQLite（data/hub.db） ── web.mjs（麦田网页 :8787）── 手机/电脑（可选 Cloudflare 隧道） │ │ │ │ └── feishu.mjs ──▶ 飞书群机器人（卡片通知） │ └───────────────────────────────────────────────┘ ``` - 平台填写逻辑在 [麦田发布助手](https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/eaaipbilkhibicihiollecmbpneikpnj)（Chrome 插件）里。插件从应用商店装进麦田的专用 Chrome 后由 Chrome 自动更新，麦田直接加载专用 Chrome 里这份插件的发布引擎（`src/plugin.mjs`），平台改版时插件更新一次，所有人自动生效。`src/chrome-shim.mjs` 在 Node 里模拟插件需要的 `chrome.tabs` / `chrome.debugger`。 - 发布工程 `publish.json` 由 `src/make-publish.mjs` 从一份 Markdown 发布素材生成，`src/validate.mjs` 校验（字数、禁词、封面比例、成片 faststart 等），字段规则跟着插件走。
命令 ```bash node src/hub.mjs plan [工程目录] # 登记进分发计划（不带目录 = 扫描 rootPath） node src/hub.mjs run <工程目录> [--only x,zsz] [--force] [--now] # 发一期；--now 让站点课程立即上线（默认推迟到定时前 30 分钟） node src/hub.mjs status [id] [--logs] node src/hub.mjs sync [--only a,b] # 取链接，写 发布记录.json，回填发布素材 md 的「已发布」行 node src/hub.mjs mark <平台> <状态> [备注] [--url 链接] # 手动改状态（平台认不出时用） node src/hub.mjs adopt <工程目录> # 登记一期已经发过的（不上传），按标题取链接 node src/hub.mjs metrics [id] # 采流量并发日报 node src/hub.mjs followers # 采粉丝 node src/hub.mjs review [天数] [--notify] # 看某期发布 N 天的复盘（守护进程会在第 1/3/7 天自动发） node src/hub.mjs weekly [--notify] # 上周周报（守护进程每周一自动发） node src/hub.mjs board # 同步到飞书多维表格（可选） node src/hub.mjs daemon # 常驻（install-launchd.sh 装的就是它） ```
配置要点（config.json） | 项 | 说明 | |---|---| | `plugin` | `store`（默认）：用专用 Chrome 里从应用商店装的麦田发布助手 | | `rootPath` / `nasUrl` | 发布工程根目录；NAS 掉线或被挂到「…-1」时守护进程会自己卸掉重挂 | | `batches` | 上传批次。一次传太多平台会互相抢带宽导致超时，建议国内两两一批 | | `auto` / `manual` | 自动提交 / 等你点发布的平台 | | `keepAlive` | 容易掉登录的平台（视频号），定时刷一下保活 | | `site` | 自有站点，可选，见下 | | `board` | 飞书多维表格看板，可选 | | `web.key` | 网页口令，所有页面和接口没有口令一律 401 |
接入你自己的站点（可选，二次开发） 不配 `config.site` 就整块关掉，网页上不显示站点卡片，「转化」页只说明怎么接。要看转化： 1. 发布 skill 会在 B站、YouTube、X 的链接上带 `utm_campaign=<主题>-<序号>`；你的站点记下访客第一次带来的这个参数，注册和下单时一起存。 2. 站点提供两个只读接口给麦田（用专用 Chrome 里的管理员登录态去调），字段见 [`src/site.mjs`](src/site.mjs) 顶部注释。 3. 在 `config.site` 里填站点地址和接口路径。 作者用自己的课程站做了示例；你的站结构不同，改 `src/site.mjs` 和转化页即可。
远程访问（可选） `scripts/install-launchd.sh --tunnel` 会装一个 cloudflared 隧道，地址推到飞书。 - **固定域名（推荐）**：域名交给 Cloudflare 后，跑 `cloudflared tunnel login`、`cloudflared tunnel create maitian`、`cloudflared tunnel route dns maitian maitian.你的域名`，在 `config.json` 里加 `"tunnel": { "name": "maitian", "hostname": "maitian.你的域名" }`。地址永远不变，建议再在 Cloudflare Zero Trust 里给它加一层邮箱验证码登录（Access → Self-hosted 应用），然后在 `config.json` 的 `web.access` 填团队域名和应用的 AUD Tag：麦田会验证 Access 签发的登录凭证，手机上输邮箱收验证码就能进，不用再带 `?key=`。 - **飞书验证码登录（推荐，零配置）**：`config.json` 的 `web` 里加 `"login": "feishu"`。远程打开麦田会先到登录页，点「发送验证码」，6 位码推到飞书群，输入后这台设备记住 30 天；验证码 5 分钟有效、只能用一次、错 5 次作废，60 秒内只能发一次。`?key=` 口令仍可用作备用。 - **快速隧道（默认）**：不配 `tunnel` 时用 `https://xxx.trycloudflare.com`，不用账号，但每次重启地址都会变。
## 手机小组件（可选） iPhone 桌面 / 锁屏常驻显示全平台粉丝、今日涨粉、最新一期播放、站点近 7 天注册和收入，点一下打开麦田。 1. `config.json` 的 `web` 里加 `"widgetToken": "<一串随机字符>"`（只读口令，只能读 `/api/widget` 的汇总数字）；想在小组件上显示头像和署名，再加 `"avatar": "data/avatar.jpg"`、`"owner": "你的名字"`（中号、大号还会显示最新一期封面） 2. 手机上登录麦田后打开 `/widget`，按页面提示装 [Scriptable](https://apps.apple.com/app/scriptable/id1405459188)、复制脚本（地址和口令已填好）。复制的是一个加载器：每次刷新从麦田的 `/api/widget/code` 拉最新的 `scripts/widget/maitian-widget.js` 来运行，以后改样式手机上自动生效，拉不到就用上次存下的那份 3. 桌面添加 Scriptable 小组件（小 / 中 / 大），锁屏也可以加（长条 / 圆形 / 单行），Script 选它 另外，Safari 里「分享 → 添加到主屏幕」可以把麦田当 App 用（全屏、带麦苗图标）。 ## 数据和隐私 - `config.json`、`data/`（数据库、日志）、`chrome-profile/`（各平台登录态）都不进 git。 - 麦田只读你自己账号的创作者后台数据，不做互动自动化、不碰别人的账号。 - 安装向导结尾、出错通知（每天最多一次）和没接站点时的「转化」页里，有一个作者知识站和交流群的链接，带 utm 参数，只是让知识站知道访客从麦田来；麦田本身不上报任何数据。不想看到就在 `config.json` 里加 `"learnLinks": false`。 ## 作者

我是麦当，做 0 基础 AI Agent / AI Coding 教程。麦田是照着我自己的发布流程一点点搭起来的，一边发视频一边在改。 - 📚 **知识站 [mdldm.club](https://www.mdldm.club/ai-course-promotion?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=maitian-readme)**：0 基础 AI Agent 课程 + 每周直播。麦田怎么搭、数据怎么采、怎么接自己的项目，课里讲得更细。 - 🎬 B站 / 小红书 / 抖音 / 视频号：搜「麦当mdldm」 - ▶️ [YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCOz23ZQMefLAgDdnraGV2RQ) · 𝕏 [@czzzzzzJ_](https://x.com/czzzzzzJ_) ### 交流群 想一起聊麦田、多平台运营的，微信扫码进群（1、2 群已满，现在开的是 3 群）：

> 微信群码 7 天有效（这张 11 月 24 日前可扫），我会定期换；扫不进去就提个 Issue 喊我一声。 觉得有用就点个 ⭐ Star，这是我继续改下去的动力；遇到问题直接提 [Issue](https://github.com/CzzzzzzJ/mdldm-maitian/issues)。 ## Star History ## License MIT

items.name: ung220z-tool
items.description: ung220z-tool 是一个针对 UNG220Z（九联/Unionman 中国移动光猫）的一键凭据提取工具，仅限在你自己的设备上用于找回忘记的管理密码、迁移宽带配置或安全自查。
items.readme:
# ung220z-tool

针对 **UNG220Z（九联 / Unionman 中国移动光猫）** 的一键凭据提取工具。

> ⚠️ 仅用于**你自己的设备**，用于找回自己忘记的管理密码、迁移宽带配置或安全自查。
> 未经授权对他人设备使用属于违法行为，作者不承担任何责任。

## 背景

这类光猫的 Web 管理页基于 `.gch` CGI 框架，登录口令由 TR-069 定期轮换，普通用户拿到的密码往往几天就失效。本工具走 Telnet 通道，直接读取设备配置库，拿到**当下有效**的全部凭据。

## 工作流程

```
用户输入账号密码
   ↓
拼出 http://<ip>/usr=<user>&psw=<pass>&cmd=1&telnet.gch 并打开浏览器（同时脚本直连兜底）
   ↓
Telnet 登录 → root shell
   ↓
sidbg 1 DB decry /userconfig/cfg/db_user_cfg.xml 解密配置
   ↓
提取 Web 账号 / Telnet 口令 / PPPoE / WiFi 密钥 / root 口令
   ↓
打印凭据表 + 落盘日志
```

## 用法

```bash
python3 ung220z.py
```

会依次询问：

```
※ 用户名和密码通常印在光猫【背面贴纸】上（S/N 标签）
  形如「用户名：user   密码：xxxxxxxx」，把光猫翻过来就能看到

① 光猫地址 [192.168.1.1]:
② 用户名 [user]:
③ 密码（输入时不显示）
   密码:
```

也可以全部走命令行：

```bash
python3 ung220z.py -i 192.168.1.1 -u user -p '你的密码'
python3 ung220z.py -i 192.168.1.1 -u user -p '你的密码' --no-browser
```

### 常用参数

| 参数 | 说明 |
|---|---|
| `-i, --ip` | 光猫地址，默认 `192.168.1.1` |
| `-u, --user` | 登录用户名，默认 `user` |
| `-p, --password` | 登录密码，不填则交互输入 |
| `--telnet-user` | Telnet 用户名，默认 `CMCCAdmin` |
| `--telnet-password` | Telnet 口令（部分机型与 Web 口令不同） |
| `--no-browser` | 不调用浏览器，纯 HTTP 请求 |
| `--unlock` | Web 被会话锁占住时重启 httpd 解锁 |
| `--no-release` | 不尝试释放残留 Web 会话 |

## 输出示例

```
[22:15:00] INFO   会话开始  目标=192.168.1.1  账户=user
[22:15:00] HTTP   已发送给浏览器: http://192.168.1.1/usr=user&psw=***&cmd=1&telnet.gch
[22:15:00] HTTP   telnet.gch → TelnetSet Success!
[22:15:00] PROBE  nc -zv 192.168.1.1 23 → succeeded
[22:15:01] AUTH   Telnet CMCCAdmin / ****** → 登录成功（root）
[22:15:02] SHELL  sidbg 1 DB decry /userconfig/cfg/db_user_cfg.xml → /tmp/debug-decry-cfg
[22:15:03] DATA   DevAuthInfo  CMCCAdmin  / ******  Level=1
[22:15:04] CRACK  MATCH: ******  (/etc/shadow)
```

最后输出凭据汇总表，并写入 `ung220z_<时间戳>.log`。

## 依赖

- Python 3.8+
- 标准库即可，无需 pip 安装
- 设备已开启 Telnet（脚本会自动通过 `telnet.gch` 尝试开启）

## 原理说明

| 环节 | 说明 |
|---|---|
| 开 Telnet | `GET /usr=<user>&psw=<pass>&cmd=1&telnet.gch`，返回 `TelnetSet Success!` 即成功 |
| Web 登录 | 密码前端只做 base64，`Frm_Logintoken` 每次响应递增，必须回填实时值 |
| 配置解密 | `sidbg 1 DB decry` 无口令即可解密，得到明文 XML |
| root 口令 | `/etc/shadow` 中为 SHA-256 crypt，工具会用常见出厂口令比对 |

## 免责声明

本项目仅用于教育与自有设备维护。使用者应确保对目标设备拥有合法管理权限。

items.name: inference-optimisation-skill
items.description: Agent skill for hill-climbing local LLM serving speed (decode, speculative decoding, prefill, KV, startup, TTFT) on any hardware and quantization
items.readme:
# inference-optimisation An agent skill for **hill-climbing the speed of a local LLM server** on any hardware and any quantization. It covers: - single-user and concurrent decode - speculative decoding - prefill - KV cache size - startup time and time to first token It works under a memory cap, and every result has to survive a full-context stability check. It encodes how we actually got these speedups. It is not a list of flags. The workflow: 1. Compute the theoretical ceiling. 2. Change one thing at a time. 3. Measure against interleaved controls. 4. Log every result, including the failures. 5. Gate on long-context retrieval. 6. Qualify a clean, pinned build before publishing. It works with Claude Code and any agent that loads `SKILL.md`-style skills. Any model can also follow it from [`PROMPT.md`](PROMPT.md). ## What we've been able to accomplish Results from the hill-climbs this skill was distilled from. Every number was measured on the hardware named; see the linked sources for methods and raw data. | Hardware | Model / quant / engine | Before → after | |---|---|---| | **Intel Arc B390 iGPU** (laptop, 64 GB unified LPDDR5X, ~115 GB/s) | Ornith-1.5-35B-A3B, EXL3 4 bpw, SGLang XPU + MTP | Decode, 1 user: 43.6 → **53 tok/s** (median)
Decode, 4 users: 84.7 → **103 tok/s**
Prefill 32K: 1,037 → **1,660 tok/s**
Prefill 256K: 297 → **628 tok/s** (2.1×)
KV cache: 264K tokens → **4 × 256K**
Startup: 113 → **43 s**
Registry Lab gates: decode 28.6 → **41.0**, prefill 255 → **667** | | **Intel Arc Pro B70** | Qwen3.8-27B, EXL3 4 bpw, vLLM + custom XPU kernels | Decode: **91.2 tok/s** at 1 user, **365** at 16 (prose, thinking on)
Same card with llama.cpp Q4_K_M: 25.0
Prefill 4K/32K/128K/254K: 1,654/1,434/928/650 → **2,421/2,259/1,415/911**
Agent-session replay: 193 → **147 s** | | **Intel Arc Pro B70** | Same model, SGLang + the same kernels | Decode, 1 user: **82.6 tok/s**, vs vLLM 75.7 on the same card and day | | **RTX 3090** | Qwen3.8-27B EXL3 3 bpw + MTP | **96.2 tok/s** prose / **141.1** code, 1 user | | **RTX 3090** | Qwen3.6-35B-A3B EXL3 3 bpw + MTP | **251.7 / 357.9 tok/s**, 1 user | | **RTX 3090** | Flash-Next EXL3, 256K context | MTP: 45.5 → **65.6 tok/s** | | **4× H200 NVL** | DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, vLLM + speculative decoding | Crashed under load → **229.1 tok/s** decode, **17,546 tok/s** prefill; all six gates pass | Sources: - [local-ai-registry](https://github.com/sybil-solutions/local-ai-registry): - [Ornith B390 recipe](https://github.com/sybil-solutions/local-ai-registry/tree/main/data/sources/ornith-b390-exl3), with the full hill-climb log in [PR #453](https://github.com/sybil-solutions/local-ai-registry/pull/453) - the RTX 3090 and H200 recipes - [trellis-serve](https://github.com/sybil-solutions/trellis-serve): - `xpu/README.md`, `xpu/docs/PROGRESS.md` and `xpu/docs/SGLANG.md` for B70 - `cuda/README.md` for the RTX 3090 - [qwen-serve](https://github.com/sybil-solutions/qwen-serve) ### Reading the B390 result That run is the one this skill grew out of. Its ceiling calculation said: - **Decode:** 100 tok/s for one user was only reachable with two useful speculative drafts. This model's draft head accepts ~14% at depth 2, so the practical target was ~88–97 tok/s. We reached ~55% of it; the rest is GEMV kernel efficiency. - **Prefill at 256K:** we reached 628 tok/s against a ~670–684 tok/s ceiling. The skill makes the agent compute this up front, so it can tell you early when a target is above the physics. ## How it works ``` ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ measure HW ─▶ │ THEORY.md: bytes/token ÷ bandwidth, FLOPs/token ÷ 50% peak, KV │ └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ baseline ─▶ profile ─▶ pick lever (ceiling gap × likelihood) ─▶ configs/NEW.json ▲ │ │ queue.sh ctl NEW ctl (serialized, AC-only, │ memory watchdog, ≥6 samples, medians) │ │ PLAN.md + ledger.jsonl ◀── accept only if it beats BOTH neighbouring controls ──┘ │ and regresses nothing by >3% ▼ long-context needle gate ─▶ concurrent full-KV soak ─▶ plateau? ─▶ pinned clean build ─▶ acceptance gates ─▶ publish ``` The skill has three parts: **[`SKILL.md`](skills/inference-optimisation/SKILL.md): the procedure.** - Inventory, ceilings, ground rules, the loop and lever order. - When to stop, how to qualify and publish, and how to report. **[`references/`](skills/inference-optimisation/references): loaded only when needed.** - [`ceilings.md`](skills/inference-optimisation/references/ceilings.md): how to compute decode, prefill, TTFT, startup and KV maxima, with a worked example. - [`methodology.md`](skills/inference-optimisation/references/methodology.md): measurement traps. Chunk-counted tokens, mis-sized prompts, acceptance counters, drift, unified-memory accounting. - [`levers.md`](skills/inference-optimisation/references/levers.md): every lever with measured evidence. It is tagged general vs stack-specific. - [`gotchas.md`](skills/inference-optimisation/references/gotchas.md): known traps in vLLM, SGLang, llama.cpp and ExLlama, and on Intel, NVIDIA, Apple and AMD hardware. - [`publishing.md`](skills/inference-optimisation/references/publishing.md): pinning, clean builds, the six acceptance gates, proving the build matches the best, results cards. **[`scripts/`](skills/inference-optimisation/scripts): a small, engine-agnostic harness.** It is standard-library Python plus bash. - `bench.py` benchmarks any OpenAI-compatible server. It measures: - startup and short-prompt TTFT; - c1 decode (median of N) and cN aggregate decode; - cold prefill at several lengths; - long-context needle retrieval; - peak memory, with a cap watchdog. It flags looping output, failed requests and runs on battery. Token counts come from server usage stats, never from streamed chunks, and everything lands in `ledger.jsonl`. - `ceiling.py` computes the theoretical ceilings from a JSON of measured bandwidth and FLOPs plus component sizes. - `queue.sh` is a serialized, detachable run queue, for interleaving control/candidate/control runs. - `mem.sh` reports a container's real footprint. That includes driver residency on unified-memory GPUs, which cgroups don't see. ## Install Claude Code (user-level): ```bash git clone https://github.com/sybil-solutions/inference-optimisation-skill mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills cp -r inference-optimisation-skill/skills/inference-optimisation ~/.claude/skills/ ``` Then ask, for example: - "hill-climb decode and prefill for the model on :8000 under a 40 GiB cap" - "what's the theoretical max tok/s for this model on this machine?" Other agents: point them at `skills/inference-optimisation/SKILL.md`, or paste [`PROMPT.md`](PROMPT.md) as the task prompt. ## Quick start without an agent ```bash S=skills/inference-optimisation python3 $S/scripts/ceiling.py $S/examples/ceiling-ornith-b390.json # ceilings mkdir -p configs && cp $S/examples/config-existing-server.json configs/base.json # edit base_url/model python3 $S/scripts/bench.py run configs/base.json --long 131072 # one run bash $S/scripts/queue.sh base cand base # interleaved A/B python3 $S/scripts/bench.py show # ledger table ``` ## Principles that carried the most weight - **Ceilings first.** If you don't know the maximum, you can't tell whether 53 tok/s is great or bad, or whether "100 tok/s" is possible. - **Noise is ±5–10%.** Most single-run "wins" are drift. Interleave controls and use medians. - **Measure what matters:** - real tokens, not stream chunks; - real prompt lengths, from the tokenizer; - real memory, including GPU residency on unified memory. - **Speculative decoding is about per-step cost, not acceptance.** - Prune the draft head's vocabulary. - Sweep draft length per concurrency and context. - Keep sampling on the GPU. - **Prove full-context stability** with exact-match needles and a concurrent full-KV soak before calling anything "best". - **Write down failures.** Most of the value in `PLAN.md` is the list of things that did *not* work and why. ## Contributing PRs with new levers, gotchas or results are welcome. Each needs the hardware, model, quantization, engine version, before → after numbers, how they were measured, and a link to raw data. ## License MIT

items.description: AI clipping for long videos and live streams. Self-hosted, bring your own AI key.
items.readme:
# PeakCut

Turn long videos and live streams into captioned vertical clips, ready to post. Free and open source: run it on
your own computer or server, with your own AI key.

Paste a YouTube, Twitch or Kick link (or upload a file) and PeakCut finds the moments worth clipping, cuts them to
9:16, adds word-by-word captions and a hook, and can post them to your connected accounts. It can also record a
creator's live stream and clip the highlights while the stream is still running.

## What it does

- **Clips from any video.** Transcribes the audio, asks an AI which moments would hold a stranger's attention, and
  renders each one with captions in one of three styles.
- **Live clipping.** Records a stream into a rolling buffer and clips as it happens, using loudness, chat activity
  and the transcript.
- **Workspaces per creator.** Channels, clip settings, posting rules and an activity log for each creator you clip.
- **Posting.** Connect YouTube, Instagram and TikTok in one click, then queue or auto-post finished clips, with
  spacing and daily caps (see [DEPLOY.md](DEPLOY.md#connecting-youtube-instagram-and-tiktok) for the one-time setup).
- **No sign-in on your own computer.** It opens straight into the dashboard. On a shared server, switch accounts on
  (`PEAKCUT_ACCOUNTS=1`) for email or Google sign-in and an admin dashboard.
- **Your own AI.** Gemini, OpenAI, Grok, Groq, OpenRouter, Claude, a local model through Ollama, or anything that
  speaks the OpenAI chat format. No key at all also works: clips are then picked by loudness.

## Quick start

You need Python 3.10 or newer and `ffmpeg`. On Windows: `winget install Gyan.FFmpeg`. On a Mac: `brew install ffmpeg`.
On Linux: `sudo apt install ffmpeg`. PeakCut finds it by itself and tells you in the dashboard if it is missing.

Put PeakCut in a short folder that stays put: `C:\peakcut` on Windows, `~/peakcut` on a Mac or Linux. Not inside a
temporary folder or an AI assistant's workspace: those get cleaned up, and on Windows a folder that deep stops the
speech model from loading (Windows can't open files whose full path is over 260 characters). If an AI assistant
installs it for you, it should ask you where to put it first ([AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) tells it to).

On Windows:

```bash
git clone <this repository> C:\peakcut
```

```bash
cd C:\peakcut
```

On a Mac or Linux:

```bash
git clone <this repository> ~/peakcut
```

```bash
cd ~/peakcut
```

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

Start the server:

```bash
python -m studio.server
```

The first start downloads the speech model by itself (about 480 MB, once).

Open http://127.0.0.1:8765. There is no sign-in: it opens straight into the dashboard. Go to **Settings, AI**, choose
your AI service, paste your key and press **Save and test** (see [Choose your AI](#choose-your-ai)).

## Choose your AI

PeakCut needs a chat model that can return JSON. The easy way is in the dashboard: **Settings, AI**. Pick the
service, paste your key, press **Find models** to choose from the service's own list, then **Save and test**. The
key is kept in the data folder on your machine and is never shown again.

If you prefer a file (or run a server), the same three things can go in `.env`. What is saved in the dashboard wins:

```ini
PEAKCUT_AI_PROVIDER=gemini
PEAKCUT_AI_MODELS=gemini-2.5-flash
PEAKCUT_AI_KEY=your-key-here
```

| `PEAKCUT_AI_PROVIDER` | Service | Where to get a key |
|---|---|---|
| `gemini` | Google Gemini | https://aistudio.google.com/apikey |
| `openai` | OpenAI | https://platform.openai.com/api-keys |
| `xai` | Grok (xAI) | https://console.x.ai |
| `groq` | Groq | https://console.groq.com/keys |
| `openrouter` | OpenRouter (many models, one key) | https://openrouter.ai/keys |
| `anthropic` | Claude | https://console.anthropic.com |
| `ollama` | A model on your own machine, no key | https://ollama.com |
| `custom` | Any OpenAI-compatible address: also set `PEAKCUT_AI_BASE_URL` | |

- `PEAKCUT_AI_MODELS` is the model id exactly as the service names it. Model names change often, so check the
  service's current list. Several ids separated by commas are tried in order, which gives you a fallback.
- A fast, inexpensive model is the right choice. A one-hour video is read in about four requests.
- You pay the AI service directly for what you use. The **AI usage** page in the app shows how many requests and
  tokens each video took.
- Speech to text does not use the AI service. It runs on your own machine, so audio never leaves it.

## Settings

Everything is set through environment variables, normally in a `.env` file next to this README.
[`.env.example`](.env.example) lists every setting with a short explanation. The ones that matter first:

| Setting | What it is for |
|---|---|
| `PEAKCUT_AI_PROVIDER`, `PEAKCUT_AI_MODELS`, `PEAKCUT_AI_KEY` | The AI that picks clips and writes titles (or set it in the dashboard) |
| `PEAKCUT_ACCOUNTS` | `1` makes everyone sign in. Use it on any server other people can reach |
| `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`, `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` | Optional: Sign in with Google, and connecting YouTube |
| `PEAKCUT_SMTP_*`, `PEAKCUT_MAIL_FROM` | Optional: confirmation and password emails |
| `PEAKCUT_DATA` | Where videos, clips and the database are kept (default `./data`) |

`.env`, the `secrets/` folder and all user data are ignored by git. Keep keys there, never in the code.

## Admins

This only matters with accounts switched on (`PEAKCUT_ACCOUNTS=1`); without them you are the owner and can do
everything. An account is an admin only when the database says so. No email address is special in the code and no web request
can change a role. Do it on the machine that runs PeakCut:

```bash
python -m studio.admin grant you@example.com
```

`revoke` and `list` work the same way. The admin dashboard is at `/admin` and answers "not found" to everyone else.

## How it is built

| Part | What it is |
|---|---|
| `studio/` | The server: FastAPI, the clip pipeline, live recording, accounts |
| `studio/ai.py` | The only file that talks to an AI service. Add a provider here |
| `web/` | The pages: landing, sign-in, the app, the admin dashboard (plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript, no build step) |
| `tests/` | Tests that run against a throwaway copy of the app |
| `deploy/`, `Dockerfile`, `docker-compose.yml` | One-server deployment with PostgreSQL and automatic HTTPS |

Video work is done with `ffmpeg` and `yt-dlp`. Speech is transcribed with `sherpa-onnx` and the Parakeet model.
Data is kept per user: accounts in the database (SQLite on your own computer, PostgreSQL on a server), videos and
clips in each user's own folder. [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) is a short map of the code for contributors and AI coding
assistants.

## Where your videos and clips are kept

Everything PeakCut keeps is in one folder: videos, clips, recordings, creators, settings and the speech model. By
default it is the `data` folder inside PeakCut. **Settings, Storage** shows the folder and how much room its drive
has, opens it in one click, and lets you move it to another drive: choose the new folder, and PeakCut moves
everything there the next time it starts. If the drive is nearly full, PeakCut says so and stops taking new videos
until there is room. (`PEAKCUT_DATA` in `.env` still works and takes priority.)

## Updating

PeakCut checks GitHub once a minute while it runs. When a newer version is out, the dashboard shows a notice
within a minute or two (no restart needed), with what changed
and how to update: ask your AI coding assistant to do it (the notice has a sentence to paste), or run
`git pull && pip install -r requirements.txt` in the PeakCut folder and restart it (with Docker:
`git pull && docker compose up -d --build`). Your `.env`, keys and clips are not touched. Only the two commit ids
are sent to GitHub; set `PEAKCUT_UPDATE_CHECK=0` to turn the check off.

## Deploy

[DEPLOY.md](DEPLOY.md) walks through a single server with Docker: the app, PostgreSQL, and Caddy for HTTPS.

```bash
docker compose up -d --build
```

## How it behaves under load

- The page asks the server one small question every few seconds. When nothing has changed, the answer comes
  straight from memory.
- Each person's videos wait in their own line and the lines take turns, so one person cannot hold everyone up.
- The server measures its own processor, memory and disk every second. Extra videos and recordings start only
  while there is room, wait briefly when it is nearly full, and continue the moment it frees up.
- There are no limits on upload size, video length, recordings, creators or storage unless you set them in
  `.env`. Five videos can be sent at once. Request sizes are always capped, so junk can't fill the memory.

## Tests

```bash
python tests/run.py
```

This starts a copy of the app on a spare port with an empty temporary data folder, runs the permission, abuse and
queue tests against it, then removes it. It needs no keys and never touches real data.

## Security

- With sign-in off, PeakCut listens on this computer only (`127.0.0.1`), refuses changes sent by other websites,
  and only answers to its own address. Do not expose it to the internet that way: turn accounts on.
- Passwords are stored only as salted scrypt hashes. Sessions are random tokens stored hashed; cookies are HTTP-only.
- Every route works out who is asking from the session, never from the request, so users only reach their own data.
- Only known video sites are fetched, and text from videos is treated as data when it is shown to the AI.
- Found a problem? Please report it privately through the repository's security advisories instead of opening a
  public issue.

## Using it responsibly

Clip videos you made, or have permission to use. You are responsible for the rights to what you download, clip and
post, and for following the terms of the sites you fetch from and post to.

## Licence

[MIT](LICENSE). Caption fonts in `studio/fonts/` (Anton, Archivo Black, Poppins) are under the SIL Open Font
License; the licence texts are in the same folder.

items.readme:
# Allo Allo is your friendly neighborhood typeface. It’s variable in weight and roundness, with proportions and curves designed to feel warm without being too cute and clear without being too cold. It’s a perfect companion out of the box, and three variable axes and plenty of alternates let you tune its personality to exactly what you need. Allo is optimized for screens and interfaces, with an optical size that adjusts automatically between text and display. And it’s packed with big little details: tabular figures, fractions, punctuation that lifts beside capitals, arrows that appear when you type them, a host of alternates and symbols, as well as a true oblique in every weight. ### [Type specimen at allo.joshpuckett.me →](https://allo.joshpuckett.me)
![Allo: the typeface, and its character set](documentation/readme-row1.png) ![Allo: OpenType features, and interface icons and symbols](documentation/readme-row2.png) ## Download Get `Allo-1.0.3.zip` from the [latest release](https://github.com/joshpuckett/allo/releases/latest): | Folder | Contents | |---|---| | `fonts/otf` | 18 static fonts, Thin to Black, each with an Oblique | | `fonts/variable` | `AlloVariable.ttf`: all optical sizes, weights and roundnesses | | `fonts/webfonts` | The same fonts as WOFF2, plus `AlloVariableFriendly.woff2` (roundness fixed at 50, about half the size) | The static and variable fonts are separate families, **Allo** and **Allo Variable**, so both can be installed. ## Web From npm: ```sh npm install allo-font ``` ```js import "allo-font"; // the full variable font, and the obliques // import "allo-font/friendly"; // or: roundness fixed at 50, about half the size ``` ```css body { font-family: "Allo", system-ui, sans-serif; } ``` Or host the files yourself, from `fonts/webfonts`: ```css @font-face { font-family: "Allo"; src: url("AlloVariable.woff2") format("woff2"); font-weight: 100 900; font-style: normal; font-display: swap; } body { font-family: "Allo", system-ui, sans-serif; } ``` - **Optical size** follows the font size (`font-optical-sizing: auto`, the CSS default). Set it to `none` to keep the Text design at every size, or pick one with `font-variation-settings: "opsz" 32`. - **Roundness** has no CSS property: use `font-variation-settings: "ROND" 0` (sharp) to `"ROND" 100` (round). Default 50. - **Smaller file:** `AlloVariableFriendly.woff2` has roundness fixed at 50; `"ROND"` has no effect. Its family name is "Allo Variable Friendly". - **Obliques:** the npm CSS includes them. Self-hosting, add an `@font-face` with `font-style: italic` and the matching `font-weight` for each oblique WOFF2 you use (`Allo-Oblique.woff2`, `Allo-BoldOblique.woff2`, …). ## Axes | Axis | Tag | Range | Default | Named values | |---|---|---|---|---| | Optical size | `opsz` | 9–32 | 14 | 9 Small, 14 Text, 32 Display | | Weight | `wght` | 100–900 | 400 | Thin 100 to Black 900 | | Roundness | `ROND` | 0–100 | 50 | 0 Sharp, 50 Friendly, 100 Round | Display (32) is tighter, with stronger optical corrections. Below 14 only the spacing changes. The static fonts are the variable font at opsz 14, ROND 50. ## OpenType features | Feature | Effect | |---|---| | `ss01` Single-story a | ɑ-shaped a | | `ss02` Disambiguation | Serifed I, tailed l, footed 1, slashed zero | | `ss03` Open figures | Open 4, 6 and 9 | | `cv01`–`cv04` | Footed 1, slashed zero, tailed l, serifed I, separately | | `cv05` | Dotted zero | | `tnum` | Tabular figures | | `zero` | Slashed zero | | `frac` | Fractions: 1/2 → ½ | | `sups`, `subs`, `numr`, `dnom` | Superscript, subscript, numerator, denominator | | `case` | Punctuation and symbols raised for capitals | | `liga` | tt, ff, tf, ft with a shared crossbar | | `calt` | `->` → →; brackets, signs, ¿ and ¡ raised beside capitals and figures | Browsers turn ligatures off when letter-spacing is set. For code, use `font-variant-ligatures: no-contextual`. ## Build Python 3.9 or newer: ```sh python3 -m venv .venv .venv/bin/python -m pip install -r requirements.txt .venv/bin/python build.py ``` Writes `fonts/` (variable TTF and WOFF2; 18 static OTFs and WOFF2s, autohinted with AFDKO), `fonts/SHA256SUMS` and `Allo-1.0.3.zip`. Dependencies are pinned and `release.json` fixes the timestamp, so builds are reproducible. ## Sources `sources/Allo.designspace` (designspace 5, UFO) has 48 masters: opsz 9, 14, 20, 32 × wght 100, 400, 580, 900 × ROND 0, 50, 100, plus eight sparse layers at ROND 10 and 30 for heavy joins. The opsz 9 masters are the opsz 14 masters with wider spacing (`release.json` "smallShift"). Corners are rounded in the outlines; the build compiles the sources as they are. Keep points compatible across masters. `sources/static` holds the 18 static fonts' sources: cut from the variable masters at opsz 14, ROND 50, then edited separately. The obliques are separate drawings, not a slant axis. ## Contributing Found a problem, or missing a character? Please [open an issue](https://github.com/joshpuckett/allo/issues); a screenshot and the text you typed help a lot. Pull requests that change the masters or the font files aren't accepted for now. Every change to a letter gets reviewed by eye across all the weights and axes, and that's hard to do well for work that arrives from outside. If you have a larger idea, such as a new script, open an issue first so we can talk about it. You're free to modify Allo and ship your own version under the [license](OFL.txt). ## License [SIL Open Font License 1.1](OFL.txt): free to use, modify and redistribute, including commercially. The fonts can't be sold by themselves. ## Credit Allo began from [Inter](https://github.com/rsms/inter) 4.2, which provided an incredible base to work from. Every one of Allo's glyphs has been redrawn, with extensive work on spacing, kerning, features and axes, all tuned for the friendly character that makes Allo its own. I owe a huge debt of gratitude to my friend [Rasmus Andersson](https://rsms.me) for creating Inter and releasing it under an open license; without it, Allo would not exist. Allo also pays homage to Honk Sans by [Seb McLauchlan](https://www.sebmclauchlan.com) and aims to bring some of that same warmth and fun to everyone.
